# Xenia Windows PowerShell Command Hygiene

This repo usually runs through Windows PowerShell 5.1. Treat it as PowerShell,
not Bash, unless the tool explicitly says otherwise.

## Hard Rules

- Do not use Bash command chaining such as `&&` or `||`.
- Do not assume Bash quoting, globbing, subshells, here-docs, `export`, `touch`,
  `cat > file`, `rm -rf`, or `/c/...` paths.
- Prefer one command per tool call. For independent reads, use
  `multi_tool_use.parallel`; for dependent steps, run a second command after
  checking the first result.
- When a single PowerShell call really needs multiple dependent steps, use
  newline-separated PowerShell statements plus explicit failure checks:

```powershell
git status --short
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
git branch --show-current
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
```

- Run repo PowerShell scripts with:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\thor\script.ps1 -Mode Example
```

- For Android Java/XML/resource-only launcher changes, prefer the fast shell
  build first:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\thor\thor_build.ps1 -Mode ApkShell -NoSubst
```

  Use `-NoSubst` for this UI loop if Gradle resource merge fails only through
  the temporary no-space drive with `!directory.isDirectory`; reserve the
  default subst path for native builds that still need no-space protection.

- Quote paths with spaces by passing arguments, `-LiteralPath`, or call
  operator syntax:

```powershell
Get-Content -LiteralPath "C:\path with spaces\file.txt" -Raw
& "C:\path with spaces\script.ps1" -Mode Status
```

- Do not pipe generated path strings into destructive commands. Resolve and
  verify paths first; use native PowerShell cmdlets with `-LiteralPath`.
- Avoid variable names that differ only by case from built-ins. For example,
  `$HOME` is read-only and PowerShell variables are case-insensitive, so `$home`
  will fail too; use names like `$codexHome` or `$repoRoot`. `$PID` is also
  read-only; use names like `$processIdText` or `$targetPid`.
- Use `Set-Content` / `Add-Content` only for generated artifacts when
  `apply_patch` is not the right tool. For repo edits, use `apply_patch`.
- For ADB commands, pass arguments as arrays when scripting and include
  `-DeviceSerial` / `adb -s <serial>` whenever more than one device could exist.
- For screenshots and binary ADB streams, use the repo helper or a known-safe
  `cmd /c "adb exec-out screencap -p > file.png"` pattern; do not pipe binary
  PNG data through PowerShell text cmdlets.

## Common Replacements

- `cmd1 && cmd2` -> two tool calls, or newline plus `$LASTEXITCODE` checks.
- `grep` -> `Select-String`; prefer `rg` for repository text search.
- `cat file` -> `Get-Content -Raw file`.
- `ls` -> `Get-ChildItem`.
- `rm -rf path` -> `Remove-Item -LiteralPath path -Recurse -Force` only after
  confirming the resolved path is inside the intended workspace.
- `VAR=value command` -> `$env:VAR = "value"` before the command, then restore
  or remove it if needed.

## Before Committing

If this skill was updated because of a command failure, leave a dated worklog
entry naming the failure class and the guardrail added. Validate with
`git diff --check`; PowerShell CRLF warnings alone are acceptable for this repo.

# Xbox 360 D3D-HLE + AOT-recompile knowledge base

## THE STRATEGIC MODEL (proven by UnleashedRecomp)
Stop emulating the Xbox 360 GPU at the PM4 command level (xenia LLE) ƒ?" that faithfully reproduces the
game's GPU inefficiencies. Instead **translate the D3D API to Vulkan directly (HLE)** + **AOT-recompile
the PPC to native**. hedge-dev's stack is the reference implementation:

- **XenonRecomp** (../reference/XenonRecomp) ƒ?" Xbox360 PPC XEX -> C++.
  - CPU state struct (`PPCContext`, XenonUtils/ppc_context.h) passed to EVERY recompiled fn; 2nd arg = base
    pointer (guest 32-bit ptrs). Instructions operate little-endian; loads/stores swap endian (marked
    volatile to stop unsafe Clang reordering). Vector regs: the WHOLE 16-byte vector is reversed (use WZY
    not XYZ in dot products, reverse args for pack). FPU keeps denormals; VMX flushes them (FP-state flag
    in the context toggled per instruction).
  - **VMX via x86 intrinsics; ARM64 via SIMDe (simd-everywhere)** => THE ARM64 PORT IS NOT FROM SCRATCH.
  - Indirect/virtual calls: perfect-hash table (fn addr*2 -> recompiled fn ptr), placed after the XEX
    region in base memory; macros in generated `ppc_config.h`.
  - Jump tables: detected by `mtctr r0` + `bctr` patterns; XenonAnalyse emits a TOML; per-game tuning.
  - Function boundaries: `.pdata` segment + heuristics; manual overrides in TOML.
  - **NO runtime provided** (you write kernel HLE + renderer + input + audio). NO exceptions. NO MMIO/XMA
    (unimplemented ƒ?" but xenia HAS an XMA decoder + full kernel HLE to port/reference).
- **XenosRecomp** (../reference/XenosRecomp) ƒ?" Xenos shader bytecode -> HLSL -> DXIL/SPIR-V (via DXC).
  - Vertex fetch: Xbox vertex DECLARATIONS -> native D3D12/Vulkan INPUT LAYOUTS (no runtime shader
    permutations); endian-swaps vertex data; 16-bit swizzle fix + R11G11B10 unpack via spec constants.
  - Constant buffers: 3 slots (VS 256 float4, PS 224 float4, shared) -> root cbuffers (D3D12) / push
    constants (Vulkan), populated from shader reflection.
  - **BYPASSES tiling / EDRAM / resolve ENTIRELY** ƒ?" the translation layer never reproduces them. THIS is
    exactly why it avoids BD's foliage-binning-doubling: it renders the scene ONCE, optimally.
- **UnleashedRecomp** (Sonic Unleashed) = the full proven port; renderer = "translation layer, not GPU
  emulation". **ReXGlue** = the same static-recompile lineage the /goal names.

## WHY THIS KILLS BD's BOTTLENECK (rigorous, from this campaign)
BD's field is GPU-bound (cpu_real 2.9ms vs 52ms GPU-fence-wait) on **foliage TRIANGLE-BINNING doubled by
predicated tiling** (2 tile passes; host_draws 940 vs rendered 675). Every xenia-LLE lever failed:
fill/MSAA/resolution (not fill-bound), naive flatten (tiles are pre-offset by the D3D RUNTIME at replay =
can't merge emulator-side), merge_draws (inapplicable), deint (inert), decimation (~25fps + artifacts,
thins foliage). HLE renders the scene ONCE (no tiling) => bin-once by construction, full foliage, correct
pixels. AOT is ORTHOGONAL: helps CPU-bound titles (Burnout/Gears) + heat; BD field GPU-bound => AOT is
thermal-only there.

## HYBRID PLAN (user-chosen 2026-07-02)
Keep xenia as the runtime base; build a D3D-HLE renderer path INSIDE it incrementally; share our existing
LLVM whole-fn backend (src/xenia/cpu/backend/llvm) as the AOT foundation. Two parallel tracks:
- TACTICAL (now): the one-tile guest patch (task #39) ƒ?" a SCOPED HLE of just BD's tiling (force tile
  count->1). Near-term correct-pixel 30fps shot within xenia.
- STRATEGIC: study how UnleashedRecomp's renderer maps Xenos draws -> Vulkan and design an xenia HLE path
  (intercept D3D draw/setrendertarget/tiling at the guest-call level instead of PM4). Start with the
  smallest surface (the tiling + main draw path) and grow.

## BD TILING MACHINERY (RE'd this campaign ƒ?" for the one-tile patch)
- Walker `0x82487878`: reads tile count `*(FUN_826bfc68()+4)`, walks cmd-list segments, per draw computes
  a per-tile predication mask vs a tile-rect table at `state+0xC` (16B/tile), writes `mask|0x80000000` to
  draw+8. (This fn CRASHED the resolution patches @0x82487948 ƒ?" delicate; changing dims desyncs the table.)
- Tiling loop `0x82487978`: gets state via `0x826BFC7C`, calls the walker per segment.
- Emitter `0x82473BD8`: writes SET_BIN_MASK/SELECT PM4 (0xc0006000/6200/6100/6300); this one resets to
  all-bins 0xffffffff. Per-tile selects (0x80000003, 0x0C) emitted in the loop.
- PATCH TARGET: where the tiling SETUP writes state+4 = tile count (2) + state+0xC = rects. Force count=1 +
  full-screen rect. NOT YET PINNED ƒ?" trace who writes state+4; state getter FUN_826bfc68 is a large fn.

## KNOWLEDGE SOURCES (the "comprehensive RAG")
- Reference source (cloned): ../reference/XenonRecomp, ../reference/XenosRecomp. (UnleashedRecomp = the
  renderer reference; clone hedge-dev/UnleashedRecomp when building the HLE renderer.)
- Xenos GPU / PM4 command reference: IN xenia's own source ƒ?" src/xenia/gpu/xenos.h (PM4 opcodes),
  packet_disassembler.cc, registers.h, the vulkan/ translator. This IS the authoritative PM4/EDRAM/resolve
  reference.
- Xbox 360 D3D9 API (XDK): the guest D3D is statically linked in each XEX (0x8246xxxx region for BD). No
  public XDK redistribution; reconstruct the API shapes from RE + the Free60/libxenon community docs +
  XenonRecomp's handling. D3DDevice_* ordinals.
- This campaign's RE artifacts: scratch/thor-debug/bd_*.txt (walker/tiling/resflow/modeflag decompiles),
  scratch/ghidra/scripts/Bd*.java.

## WORKFLOW
- RE a game's tiling/surface: Ghidra headless (see xenia-thor-ghidra-game-patch skill) on the XEX; find
  SET_BIN_SELECT emitter via the PM4 header constants (ori 0x6200/6300/6000/6100); decompile the walker +
  its callers; trace the tile-count writer.
- Design an HLE intercept: identify the guest D3D fn (statically linked, by ordinal/behavior), decide
  whether to (a) PATCH it (.patch.toml, cheapest ƒ?" e.g. tile count->1), or (b) HLE-replace it (patch entry
  to trampoline into a host impl ƒ?" the real translation layer).
- Validate: device A/B (single-run alternating for perf; screenshot for pixels); the alternator-gated
  method (gpu_freeze_ab_alternate_vrs phase) is the rigorous perf harness.

## ƒo. PROVEN REƒ+'HLE RECIPE (2026-07-03) ƒ?" reusable across games, this is THE fast path
The "reach in, pin the D3D fn, HLE it" loop, validated on BD's tiling replay. Four committed tools:

**1. PIN the D3D fn that writes a target struct ƒ?" PAGE-WATCH (`cpu_watch_guest_write_page`, a64_backend.cc
ExceptionCallback + processor.cc walker-protect).** The store-watch (`arm64_guest_store_watch`) FAILS on the
field (per-store JIT emit = ~10x slowdown ƒ+' timed nav desyncs). The page-watch has ZERO per-store cost: host-
mprotect the target guest page read-only; on write-fault, **emulate-on-fault** (decode store size[31:30]+Rt
[4:0], do the write to ex->fault_address() yourself, keep protected = no un-protect windows = catch EVERY
write) + `code_cache->LookupFunction(ex->pc())` ƒ+' the writer guest fn + `ctx->lr` (PPCContext @ host x[20]) ƒ+'
its CALLER. Runs BD full-speed ƒ+' reaches the field. THIS is the tool the multi-session RE wall needed.

**2. Peel helper wrappers.** Writers are often memcpy(0x826bf770)/calloc(0x8246B3B8) helpers; the real D3D fn
is the CALLER ƒ?" read `ctx->lr` in the page-watch hit. calloc/memcpy have NO static refs (deep indirect) so
static Ghidra caller-analysis is DEAD; the runtime page-watch lr is the only way.

**3. GOTCHA ƒ?" xenia's DECLARED entry ƒ%ÿ Ghidra prologue.** BD's tiling replay: Ghidra prologue-scan said
0x82487cc8, but xenia harvested it as **0x82487CC0-82487F50** (grep logcat `shared-fn-harvest`). HLE the
xenia-DECLARED entry (0x82487CC0), else `IsHleIntercept` never matches ƒ+' planted=0. Also: fns reached by
tail-call/indirect (driver 0x82487988) are NEVER LookupFunction'd ƒ+' un-plantable; only harvested entries plant.

**4. HLE HOST BODY ƒ?" reimplement the D3D fn (`cpu_hle_tiling_replay_addr`, processor.cc HleTilingReplayHandler).**
SetupExtern at LookupFunction plants the host handler (kExtern dispatch, no guest-code patch). For a REPLAY/
token-loop fn, reimplement the loop in host C++, reading the recorded stream (r3) + ctx (r4) with load/store_
and_swap (BE), and calling guest helpers (ring writer 0x8246E100, tiling helpers) REENTRANTLY via
`Processor::Execute(ThreadState::Get(), addr, args[], n)` (argsƒ+'r[3+i], returns r[3]; keep your loop state in
C++ LOCALS since Execute clobbers ctx->r). VIABLE: only ~dozens of setup PM4 emits/frame (draws go via the
driver/walker, not the tiling-setup fn). Device: **planted+faults=0 = the host body IS the D3D fn + runs**.
Then apply the bin-once tweak (force tile count=1) + the COHERENT surface rewrite (RB_SURFACE_INFO pitch +
color/depth EDRAM bases + resolve TOGETHER ƒ?" piecemeal downstream override = 0fps black EDRAM desync; that's
why HLE-at-SOURCE beats RT-cache coalescing). VdGlobalDevice ptr = *(0x820005f4).

## dY?-‹,? LOAD-TIME XEX PIPELINE (RPCS3-model endgame ƒ?" the user's "progress bar" vision)
The right architecture = at GAME LOAD, a progress-bar pass that (a) AOT-LLVM-compiles the PPC (we HAVE the
object cache: [[llvm-jit-backend-build]], `cpu_backend_llvm` + AOT .o cache), and (b) SIGNATURE-scans the XEX
for the static-linked XDK D3D9 fns ƒ+' installs HLE trampolines (the mechanism above), caching both keyed by
XEX hash. RPCS3 analog: its boot progress bar AOT-recompiles PPU/SPU modules; we AOT the PPC + (the SPUƒ+'HLE
analog) signature-identify + host-replace the D3D fns. This = build-order step 4 (a signature DB stable per
XDK version 2005-2013, generic across games ƒ?" NOT a per-game port). EDRAM is THE core inefficiency; HLE-ing
BeginTiling/Resolve bypasses the predicated tiling + EDRAM round-trip AT THE SOURCE = render once / resolve
once. To generalize: the page-watch recipe pins BeginTiling/Resolve/Draw per game; their SIGNATURES (byte
patterns of the harvested fn) go in the DB; the loader matches + trampolines them without re-RE.

# Xenia Vulkan Adreno RenderDoc

Use this skill when logs show real GPU traffic, PM4 packets, draw calls,
writeback waits, or black output after Vulkan setup.

## First Rule

RenderDoc is a GPU frame tool, not proof that guest CPU execution is correct.
Only use it after normal logcat proves a meaningful guest GPU frame path.
For this fork, AYN Thor Adreno proof matters more than Windows renderer proof,
but CPU/A64 speed evidence still outranks GPU deep dives when the profile says
the guest CPU is the wall.

## Mature Vulkan Port Bias

Use `docs/research/20260524-165737-mature-vulkan-port-speed-design.md` as the
GPU design ladder, and `docs/research/20260524-171203-vulkan-counter-surface-audit.md`
as the repo-local counter surface map. Other mature emulator Vulkan ports
converge on the same shape:

- device and driver profile before optional Vulkan behavior;
- console GPU milestone classification before frame tools;
- deterministic trace/replay before broad renderer edits;
- shader/pipeline cache timing before async compilation or prewarming;
- EDRAM, resolve, texture-cache, and writeback correctness before speed claims;
- explicit queue/fence/present wait attribution before "push more GPU" work;
- validation, RenderDoc, AGI, and quiet FPS captures kept as separate lanes.

For Blue Dragon, do not start broad GPU work while quiet captures still show the
main CPU/JIT thread as the wall. A GPU slice needs fresh evidence such as high
GPU wait, resolve/copy body cost, shader/pipeline stalls, present pacing stalls,
or a real black-frame milestone regression.

Before a GPU speed patch, run the no-behavior audit:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\thor\thor_vulkan_counter_surface_audit.ps1
```

The current default-off counter skeleton is documented in
`docs/research/20260524-173639-vulkan-perf-counter-skeleton.md`. Enable it
through `tools\thor\thor_xenia_debug.ps1` with
`-VulkanTracePerfCounters true -VulkanTracePerfCountersLogInterval <N>`. It
already logs IssueSwap, graphics pipeline create/cache-hit, queue submit,
present acquire/submit/present, barriers, and render-pass starts. Prefer a
route-stabilized control/counter sandwich over a renderer rewrite until Thor
route metadata proves whether the GPU wall is pipeline creation, queue/present,
barriers, readbacks/uploads/copies, descriptor churn, resolves, or completion
waits.

The first route-clean counter sandwich is
`docs/research/20260524-175206-vulkan-counter-route-sandwich.md`. Both control
and counter-on captures reached the visible opening sky/dragon-wing route with
clean fatal-marker searches. The counter-on run had `issue_swaps=840`,
`pipeline_creates=56`, `barrier_submits=115307`, `present_failures=0`, and no
queue submit failures, while Main Thread stayed near one full core and GPU
Commands stayed low. Treat this as evidence to keep the main sprint CPU/A64
biased, not as permission for a broad Vulkan rewrite.

## Normal Evidence Search

```powershell
rg -n "VdSwap|PM4_XE_SWAP|XE_SWAP|Vulkan IssueSwap|guest output callback|RequestSwapTexture|EVENT_WRITE_SHD|WAIT_REG_MEM|COND_WRITE|DRAW_INDX|CommandProcessor ExecutePrimaryBuffer|read pointer writeback|GPU is hung" scratch\thor-debug\*-logcat.txt
```

Classify:

- no `VdSwap`: guest/kernel/video path has not requested present.
- `VdSwap` but no `PM4_XE_SWAP`: ring buffer or command generation issue.
- `PM4_XE_SWAP` but no `Vulkan IssueSwap`: command processor dispatch issue.
- `Vulkan IssueSwap` but black screen: texture cache, render target, presenter,
  or Adreno/Vulkan path.
- watchdog with real PM4 draws: guest-visible completion/writeback semantics or
  shader/pipeline compile latency.

## Files To Inspect

- `docs/gpu.md`
- `src/xenia/gpu/command_processor.cc`
- `src/xenia/gpu/command_processor.h`
- `src/xenia/gpu/gpu_flags.*`
- `src/xenia/gpu/registers.h`
- `src/xenia/gpu/xenos.h`
- `src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc`
- `src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_texture_cache.cc`
- `src/xenia/ui/vulkan/vulkan_presenter.cc`
- `src/xenia/kernel/xboxkrnl/xboxkrnl_video.cc`

Run `.agents/skills/xenia-thor-experiment-gate/SKILL.md` first for risky GPU
toggles so the probe has one primary variable and a rollback story.

Start with:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\thor\thor_xenia_debug.ps1 -Mode LaunchBlueDragon -DeviceSerial c3ca0370 -GpuTraceSwap true -GpuTracePacketBudget 260 -GpuInterruptOnRingIdle false -GpuBlueDragonKickWaitToken false
```

Only enable experimental knobs one at a time:

- `-GpuEarlyPrimaryReadPointerWriteback true`
- `-ClearMemoryPageState true`
- `-GpuInterruptOnRingIdle true`
- `-GpuBlueDragonKickWaitToken true`

Document why each knob is enabled and what invariant it tests.


immediately after the capture attempt.

## Adreno Caution

- Keep Vulkan validation and RenderDoc runs separate from normal performance
  captures.
- Treat shader/pipeline compile latency as a possible guest watchdog trigger.
- If the screen is black, prove whether the guest frontbuffer contains useful
  data before blaming Android presentation.
- Treat Adreno as a tile-based mobile target: minimize unnecessary
  external-memory round-trips, use precise load/store intent where the current
  render-target path permits it, and avoid optional format or extension
  assumptions without Thor feature logs.
- Do not report fork-specific Vulkan findings upstream unless reproduced on an
  official Xenia build.

## Output

- first missing GPU milestone,
- PM4/writeback/presenter evidence,
- exact capture path,
- next GPU experiment and cvars,
- whether RenderDoc or AGI is justified now.

## How to run it

### 1. Write the prompt file
Assemble ONE self-contained prompt (the models have no repo/memory context). Put it in
`scratch/consult/problem.txt` (scratch/ is gitignored). It MUST include:
- The problem + the concrete ask.
- The relevant device-measured facts and the **proven walls** (so they don't re-derive dead ends).
  For Thor speed problems, prepend `docs/research/20260616-thor-speed-problem-briefing.md`.
- The default "hard rethink" instruction block (below).

Default instruction block to append to the problem:
```
You are a world-class systems/emulator/GPU engineer giving an INDEPENDENT second opinion.
Do three things, clearly separated:
1. RED-TEAM: attack the current plan/conclusion below ƒ?" find the flawed assumption, the missed
   case, the reason it is wrong or won't deliver. Be specific and technical.
2. ALTERNATIVES: ignore our framing and propose 2-3 fundamentally different approaches from first
   principles, with the concrete mechanism and the expected payoff/risk of each.
3. VERDICT: the single highest-value thing to try next and why, plus what would falsify it.
Do not flatter. If our analysis is right, say so and sharpen it. Cite specifics over generalities.
```

### 2. Run BOTH in parallel (long-running ƒ?" use a 600000 ms timeout or run_in_background)
Preferred (helper does the parallel fan-out + capture):
```
.\.agents\skills\consult-hard\consult.ps1 -PromptFile scratch\consult\problem.txt -OutDir scratch\consult
```
Outputs: `scratch/consult/codex.md` and `scratch/consult/gemini.md`.

Raw equivalents (if you'd rather run them as two separate background calls):
```powershell
Get-Content scratch\consult\problem.txt -Raw | codex exec -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high" --skip-git-repo-check - *>&1 | Out-File scratch\consult\codex.md -Encoding utf8
Get-Content scratch\consult\problem.txt -Raw | gemini -m gemini-3-flash-preview 2>$null | Out-File scratch\consult\gemini.md -Encoding utf8
```
(Gemini prints a harmless "256-color" warning to stderr ƒ?" `2>$null` keeps the captured answer clean.)

### 3. Reconcile (this is the point ƒ?" don't just relay)
Read both files. Then to the user, produce:
- **Where they agree** (highest-confidence signal).
- **Where they disagree / disagree with us** (the interesting part ƒ?" adjudicate it with our
  device-measured facts; the external models do NOT have our measurements, so reject any claim
  that contradicts a proven wall and SAY why).
- **The one or two concrete next actions** you'll take, and what each would prove.
Treat their output as hypotheses to verify against the device/code, never as ground truth.

## Gotchas
- **Long prompts go in a FILE piped via stdin**, never as a quoted arg (PowerShell quoting + size).
- **Max reasoning is slow** (minutes). Always long-timeout or background; never a 120 s default.
- `*>&1` captures the streamed reasoning + the answer; for Codex you can use `-o file` to get only
  the final message. Write outputs under `scratch/` (gitignored) ƒ?" they can be large.
- The models are stateless across calls ƒ?" every consult re-sends full context.
- These are **advisors**. The project's rules still bind: device-measured facts win, no fabrication,
  validate IN-GAME, forward-only. An external suggestion is a lead to test, not a result.
- Free Gemini tier is rate-limited (~60/min, 1000/day); Codex uses the user's ChatGPT plan quota.

# NATIVE RENDER PATH ƒ?" the BD GPU-pipeline REARCH (not a lever)

**WHY (user-mandated 2026-07-04, "NO MORE INCREMENTAL LEVERS, REARCH"):** BD's ~15-20A- emulation gap is a
COMPOUNDING STACK of ~2A- emulation taxes, not one bug. Every single-layer lever (native-fetch, blend-bind
collapse, resolution, EDRAM elision) read FLAT because removing ONE layer leaves the other four dominating.
The rearch removes the WHOLE stack ƒ+' the compound 10-20A- ƒ+' 30-60fps. **RULE: build + measure the COMPOUND,
never one layer (that's the trap that killed every lever).** The Thor is 10-20A- the 360; the 360 hit 30 by
rendering NATIVELY. We render the scene natively too.

## The stack (each ~2A-, multiplying)
1. **SSBO in-shader vertex fetch** (vs native HW input assembly) ƒ?" `gpu_hw_vertex_fetch` BUILT (flat alone).
2. **1272 state-changes/frame** (208 pipeline + 1064 descriptor binds) each context-rolling the TBDR ƒ?" BINDLESS not built.
3. **EDRAM round-trips across 42 render passes** (vs GMEM-resident single pass) ƒ?" RT-cache exists, not the native path.
4. **Xenosƒ+'SPIR-V shader bloat** (~1.5A-) + fp32 where fp16 suffices ƒ?" Adreno FP16 unused for foliage.
5. **Format/bandwidth waste** (fp16 64bpp color, no native format match) ƒ?" quality-option fp10 only.

## Build order (each brick STACKS on the prior; measure the compound at each stack point)
- **BRICK 0 ƒo. native vertex input** ƒ?" `gpu_hw_vertex_fetch` (buffer bound as VkBuffer, native shader attrs via
  kSysFlag_HwVertexFetch, fixed-function VkVertexInputState in the pipeline). Exists; keep, don't re-measure alone.
- **BRICK 1 dY"" BINDLESS resources** (descriptor_indexing + buffer_device_address, both device-confirmed) ƒ?" ONE
  global texture array (runtimeDescriptorArray + partiallyBound + VARIABLE_DESCRIPTOR_COUNT), bound ONCE/frame;
  shaders index it by push-constant instead of per-draw descriptor sets. Collapses the 1064 descriptor binds ƒ+'
  ~0 AND removes the per-texture pipeline variance ƒ+' fewer of the 208 pipeline binds. Current per-draw path to
  replace: GetTextureDescriptorSetLayout (vulkan_command_processor.cc:4545) + the per-draw CmdVkBindDescriptorSets
  (:3615) built from pixel_shader->texture_bindings() (:5130). Gate: `gpu_native_render_path` (compound cvar).
- **BRICK 2 native render targets** ƒ?" render the scene to a GMEM-resident image via dynamic_rendering +
  dynamic_rendering_local_read (device-confirmed) once, read composites in-place; bypass the EDRAM tile round-trip
  across the 42 passes. Build on the RT cache.
- **BRICK 3 lean fp16 shaders** ƒ?" Xenosƒ+'SPIR-V with RelaxedPrecision/fp16 for the foliage fragment path (Adreno
  native FP16 throughput) + drop the bloat.

## Measurement discipline (the anti-lever rule)
Enable BRICKS 0+1 TOGETHER, then 0+1+2, then all ƒ?" measure the COMPOUND frame time + OSD fps at each stack point,
never a brick alone. One-brick A/B is meaningless here (the stack hides it). Single-run, GPU-busy field, screenshot-
correct. The compound is the only honest signal.

## Status
- BRICK 2: BUILT + DEVICE-TESTED 2026-07-04 (gpu_native_render_targets). **DEAD.** cap=1 renders DOUBLED
  (two Shus/windmills - the host image is 1-sample = half the tile footprint the guest addresses at guest-MSAA,
  so content WRAPS; the guest-footprint-ownership fix doesn't decouple host-storage-samples from EDRAM-addressing-
  samples, the real fix) AND fps FLAT (18.6 vs shipped 19.8, ~52ms vs ~50ms) = cap=2 already captured the MSAA
  win; cap=1 adds nothing. The "cap=1 = ƒ^'42%" was a CONFOUNDED cross-run number. Kept default-off. The clean
  storage/addressing decouple (multisample views threaded through resolve/transfer shaders) is the only fix and
  it's large + risky, and the payoff is FLAT ƒØ' not worth it. Fragment MSAA lever is closed.
- BRICK 0: shipped (default-off), FLAT alone.
- BRICK 1: BUILT + DEVICE-TESTED 2026-07-04 (gpu_native_render_path). Renders PIXEL-PERFECT (bindless
  architecture correct, no crash) BUT **REGRESSED: 129ƒ+'161ms / 7.7ƒ+'6.2fps, and descriptor_binds UNCHANGED
  (~1074), pipeline_binds UNCHANGED (208).** Decisive finding: **the 1064 descriptor binds are NOT texture
  binds ƒ?" they are set-0 (shared-mem) + set-1 (per-draw CONSTANTS), inherent per-draw data bindless can't
  touch; the 208 pipeline binds are shader/render_pass variants. So the "1272 state-change tax" is NOT
  collapsible via bindless textures** ƒ?" bindless removed the small texture-bind slice + ADDED push-constant/
  indirect overhead ƒ+' net regression. Compound (BRICK0+1) REGRESSES.

## dYs" THE REARCH PREMISE IS REFUTED BY THE FRAME ANATOMY (2026-07-04)
The driver u_trace already said BD's frame = **~90% fragment/draw EXECUTION (the intrinsic foliage rendering),

# BD native D3D9Г+'Vulkan renderer (DXVK-for-360) Г?" build blueprint (2026-07-05)

## Why (RE2 proof + amplification math, all device-measured this session)
RE2 Remake (far heavier) runs 30fps on the Thor via DXVK Г+' the Adreno 740 is NOT the wall; xenia's LLE
emulation is. BD's heavy field = **n=95 render passes** (16 geometry + 35 EDRAM-xfer + 23 resolve + 18
composite); gpu_pass_usГ%^4ms yet gpu_frame_usГ%^123ms. The ~119ms is the foliage fragment work AMPLIFIED by the
emulation. The amplification factors (measured/derived), multiplicative Г%^ 9A-:

| factor | A-    | source | native renderer removes it by |
|--------|------|--------|-------------------------------|
| per-tile re-execution | 2A- | BD's 2 EDRAM tiles each re-shade the region | render ONCE into one full-surface RT (no tiling) |
| foliage self-overdraw | ~3A- | 43% overdraw + no early-Z reject (discard defeats LRZ + LOAD_OP_LOAD kills it) | clean single depth pass Г+' forced per-pixel EarlyFragmentTests works (gpu_foliage_force_early_z, built) against a foliage-primed depth |
| ir3 shader bloat | ~1.5A- | XenosГ+'ir3 translation | native/optimized SPIR-V (or accept; smallest factor) |
| pass/barrier/xfer overhead | (part of the above gaps) | 79 EDRAM overhead passes | native RT triggers NO ownership-transfer/resolve passes |

Removing tiling (2A-) + enabling reject (~3A- on the occluded half) + fewer passes Г+' target ~3A- Г+' ~40ms Г+' the
VRS/ir3 headroom closes to 30fps. **This is the whole-pipeline conversion; no single factor alone suffices
(proven Г?" every isolated lever is DEAD in the exp_ledger).**

## What (the renderer)
A cvar-gated (`gpu_bd_native_renderer`, default-off) native Vulkan path for BD's field, PARALLEL to the LLE
back-end (LLE stays the correctness fallback / other games):
1. **Capture** at the RE'd seam **0x82489F40** (SubmitRectDraw Г?" ONE call per game draw, PRE per-tile fan-out).
   State in device-ctx **dev+0x2800..0x2938** (bound shaders/RT/blend), dev+0x2F88 surface/viewport, dev+0x3058
   scissor, dev+(binIdx+0xBE2)*4 per-bin surface. Infra exists (decoupled native-HLE capture + CallInThread
   handoff to the CP worker thread).
2. **Own RT**: one persistent full-surface `VkImage` (720A-1280-ish, native, NOT EDRAM-backed) + one depth image.
   Allocated once, reused. This is the change render_target_cache.cc:642 warns against doing IN the EDRAM path Г?"
   so do it OUTSIDE it (a dedicated image the native path owns).
3. **Own render pass**: ONE (or few) VkRenderPass, held open across all captured draws (no per-RT-change breaks =
   no xfer/resolve passes). Optional depth-prepass sub-step so EarlyFragmentTests rejects self-overdraw.
4. **Native pipelines**: reuse xenia's XenosГ+'SPIR-V translator for the shaders, but bind via native
   VkPipelineVertexInputState (real VkBuffer vertex data, NOT the SSBO vfetch) + native VkPipelineColorBlendState
   (hardware ROP). Cache pipelines by state hash (DXVK model).
5. **Present**: blit the native RT to the swapchain (present_decoupled infra exists).

## Build order (implement on DESKTOP **VULKAN** Г?" `xenia.exe --gpu=vulkan` Г?" SAME backend as Turnip, ships direct; then device)
> User mandate 2026-07-05: "use vulkan on desktop". Dev on the desktop Vulkan backend (RenderDoc to inspect pass
> count/pipelines, iterates in seconds), so the VkImage/VkRenderPass/VkPipeline/SPIR-V code is IDENTICAL to what
> runs on the Thor's Turnip Г?" NO rewrite. D3D12 would be throwaway. Then MSBuild the Android APK + measure fps.
- **Brick 1**: allocate the persistent native color+depth image + one render pass; render a single captured

- **Brick 3**: depth-prepass + gpu_foliage_force_early_z Г+' self-overdraw reject. Measure the 3A- on the occluded half.

  reads. Validate render correctness (screenshot) + lock the fps.

## Anti-repeat (do NOT redo Г?" exp_ledger has the data)
Decoupled native-HLE = PERF-FLAT (kept xenia's 95-pass back-end Г?" the whole point is to NOT keep it). Bin-once/
force-1-tile, in-pass, skip-transfers, downscale, MSAA, ROAA, ALL early-Z/LRZ levers on the LLE path = DEAD.
FSI/interlock = ABSENT on Turnip. The renderer is the ONLY remaining axis.

## Brick 2b Г?" concrete integration map (verified in code 2026-07-05, the 3 real layers)
Rendering BD's field geometry into the native RT is NOT a redirect one-liner. Three coupled layers, each real:
1. **Pipelines**: `VulkanPipelineCache::ConfigurePipeline` is keyed to `VulkanRenderTargetCache::RenderPassKey`
   (vulkan_pipeline_cache.h:82-90) - it only builds pipelines for the EDRAM render passes. Two options: (a) build
   native pipelines directly from the translated `VulkanShader` SPIR-V modules (SSBO vertex-fetch, no vertex-input)
   against `render_pass_`; (b) make the native render pass FORMAT-COMPATIBLE with the field's RenderPassKey so the
   cache's pipelines are reusable (Vulkan: load/store ops don't affect compat, only formats/samples - vulkan_cmd_
   processor.cc:4199-4202). (b) is less code IF the native RT format == field color format (RB_COLOR_INFO; test
   k_8_8_8_8=RGBA8, my native RT is RGBA8 = likely compatible).
2. **Framebuffer**: the draw path's `current_framebuffer_` is `const VulkanRenderTargetCache::Framebuffer*` (a
   WRAPPER, vulkan_cmd_processor.h:1889), set at :4197 next to `current_render_pass_` (VkRenderPass, raw). Redirect
   = override both there for field draws (pitch 720 via RB_SURFACE_INFO&0x3FFF), but need a Framebuffer WRAPPER
   around the native VkFramebuffer (or special-case the CmdVkBeginRenderPass at :4340 to use the raw handle).
   Getter `BdNativeRenderer::framebuffer()` added.
3. **Tiling collapse**: BD fans the field out per-tile (2 tiles top 0..672 / bottom 608..1280, window offsets).
   Redirecting alone renders BOTH tiles into the native RT (2x, mispositioned). Must force count=1 + ignore window
   offset + full-surface scissor (the bin-once, but into the CLEAN native RT instead of the format/scissor-fighting
   EDRAM RT - the native RT may sidestep what broke bin-once). THIS is the actual perf win (collapses the passes).
NEXT: (b) format-match native RT to field + redirect + bin-once-into-native-RT, on desktop --gpu=vulkan (RenderDoc:
verify one pass + BD geometry), then Thor-measure. The native RT+pass+present is PROVEN (magenta on Turnip); this is
the draw-into-it path.

## STATUS 2026-07-05 (device-confirmed) Г?" BD GEOMETRY RENDERS NATIVELY (Brick 2b done), perf-collapse remains
**WIN (bd_twopass.png, Turnip):** BD's actual field (Shu + foliage + terrain + buildings + props) RENDERS NATIVELY

3. **Two-pass accumulate** (the black-render fix): the pass RE-BEGINS mid-frame (non-720 draws break it); UNDEFINED
   initialLayout + LOAD_OP_CLEAR wiped the accumulated geometry each re-begin Г+' black. Fix = TWO render passes (same
   attachments, both framebuffer-compatible): **CLEAR pass** (init UNDEFINED) for the FIRST field draw of a frame,
   **LOAD pass** (init=final=SHADER_READ / depth-attachment, loadOp=LOAD, depth storeOp=STORE) for ALL re-begins Г+'
   geometry ACCUMULATES. Redirect selects clear-vs-load via `bd_native_field_rendered_`.

- **Do NOT regress:** the two-pass accumulate + format/samples/depth match + redirect are the working foundation.

## STATUS 2026-07-06 Г?" REAL-HLE (EDRAM-deletion) SUBSTRATE BUILT + COMPILING (desktop)
The partial HLE renders only the FIELD natively; shadows/RT-textures stay in EDRAM, and the 35 ownership
transfers (~110ms) are LOAD-BEARING because the field samples that EDRAM content. The real HLE deletes EDRAM by
giving each logical surface its OWN persistent VkImage keyed by its guest RESOLVE-DEST address (the stable D3D9
resource identity, DXVK/Cemu model) Г?" rendered into AND sampled directly, so no transfers. Built this session

- **Brick A Г?" native-surface registry** (`bd_native_renderer.h/.cc`): `struct NativeSurface` (own color+depth
  image/views/2 passes[CLEAR+LOAD]/framebuffer, single-sample) + `std::unordered_map<uint32_t key, NativeSurface>
  surfaces_`. API: `AcquireSurface(key,w,h,color_fmt,depth_fmt,samples)` (get-or-create, persistent, rebuild on
  cfg change), `FindSurface`, `LookupSampledSurface(guest_addr)` (returns color_view ONLY once color_layout==
  SHADER_READ = real content, else nullГ+'EDRAM fallback), `BeginSurfaceFrame`, `surface_count`. Registry freed in
  the DESTRUCTOR (NOT Shutdown Г?" EnsureColorFormat reuses Shutdown for the primary RT and must not wipe surfaces).
- **Brick B Г?" native texture-fetch redirect (CONSUME side)** (`vulkan_command_processor.cc` UpdateBindings, right
  after the `gpu_rt_as_texture` block ~10778): for each pixel fetch, `GetActiveTextureGuestInfo(fc,&base,&fmt)` Г+'
  `bd_native_renderer_->LookupSampledSurface(base)`; if non-null, write it into `rt_as_texture_views_pixel_[fc]`
  (the SAME override array the descriptor-write loop at ~10939 already binds). Gated `gpu_bd_native_renderer &&
  surface_count()>0`. No-op until a surface holds content = safe/non-breaking. THIS is the DXVK-style
  render-to-texture bind: field samples the native image, not the EDRAM upload.
- **Brick C1 Г?" persistent resolve graph** (`vulkan_command_processor.h` AddResolveCopyStats): `persistent_resolve_
  edges_` (unordered_map<NativeSrcKey(src_edram_base_tiles,is_depth), ResolveEdge>), populated every resolve (the

# BD EDRAM-deletion Г+' 30fps: executable build plan (2026-07-08)

## The proven mechanism (why EDRAM deletion IS the 30fps path)
- BD's field is **GPU-fragment-bound**: 25.2fps, GPU 99% @ max clock 680MHz on the full BD GameProfile (VRS4 + fp10 + MSAA2 + clamp) + AOT. (profbound.ps1)
- The fragment cuts that reach 30fps **resize the render target** and **garble on the EDRAM tile model**:
  - MSAA 2Г+'1 (Г^'28%): 22.2fps + garble (profm1.ps1).
  - resolution downscale 85%: 26fps + heavy garble (profds.ps1).
  - Cause: BD's 2A--packed main-scene RT bases are re-derived wrong at reduced size in the EDRAM tile addressing (the "cap=1 footprint mismatch", bd-edram-atomic-rop-solve).
- Levers that DON'T resize the RT (VRS4, fp10) render clean but cap at 25fps.
- **Native resource-keyed RTs bypass EDRAM addressing Г+' the resized RTs render clean Г+' MSAA1/downscale unlock Г+' 30fps.** This is the confirmed reason to delete EDRAM.
- Dead ends (do not retry): naive early-Z `gpu_foliage_force_early_z` (22.7fps + white-band, profez.ps1); foliage decimation (user: never).

## What already works (PC-verified)
- Field renders **correct on desktop** with `gpu_bd_native_renderer` + `gpu_bd_native_aux_rt` + `gpu_bd_native_aux_fmt37=false` + `drop_resolves` + `drop_transfers` (desk_hle54.png, desk_mainscene.png). EDRAM resolves + color transfers deletable on PC, field correct.
- AOT object cache shipped default-on (EmulatorActivity.java onCreate ~line 207); warm launches skip the ~32% LLVM compile.
- `gpu_clamp_rt_image_height=768` (BD profile) clamps RT image to actual rows Г+' native-size RTs (tile-I/O minor).

The key conclusions are:

1. `rt_transfers` currently does not measure transfers that survive the drop gate, so the apparent intermittent bloom dropping is probably a measurement artifact.
2. `copy_dest_exp_bias=-2` is resolve-side. Your native conversion must apply it.
3. Use a fullscreen graphics conversion pass: a normal offline-built `.ps.xesl`, MSAA sampled-image input, and A2B10 color-attachment output. This is the least-risk Turnip path.

## 1. Drop reliability

The current counter is counted before `BdL5DropSafe` clears transfer vectors. `AddRenderTargetTransferStats` sees the requested transfers around [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6526](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6526>), while the L5 filtering and `clear()` happen later around [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6566](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6566>).

Therefore:

```text
rt_transfers = transfers requested before filtering
```

It is not:

```text
rt_transfers = transfers actually executed
```

In the current [brick1_l9trace.log](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/scratch/blue-dragon/brick1_l9trace.log>), the `35` values occur in the earlier workload; the steady field is predominantly `45`. The native-consumer records for the five observed field/bloom destinations are themselves stable. That does not prove the transfers dropped, because the counter cannot answer that question.

Instrument these three numbers first:

```text
rt_transfers_requested
l5_transfer_entries_dropped
rt_transfers_executed
```

Increment `dropped` immediately before clearing the vector, and calculate `executed` after all filtering. Also log:

```text
dest canonical key
generation

previous consumer bits
drop verdict
failure reason
```

### Why the existing census is still unsafe

Even if the missing-entry premise disappears, the current gate is not fully fail-closed:

- The native bit is recorded only after every redirect check succeeds in [vulkan_command_processor.cc:11354](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:11354>). Signedness, epoch, format, missing image, or swizzled-view failures exit without recording anything.
- In pure LLE, those fallback exits do not consistently set `kNonNative`; the relevant fallback marking is associated with the inactive native-renderer branch.
- `dest_base` is not a resource identity. Different dimensions, pitches, formats, mips, tiled state, or generations may reuse it.
- `persistent_resolve_edges_[src_rt_key] = edge` stores only one destination. BD can resolve one source RT to multiple bloom destinations, so the later edge overwrites the earlier one.
- A downsample chain can genuinely be mixed: one exact fetch may redirect, while another fetch of the same base with a different shape/mip/format falls back to LLE.

The decision on your options is:

- **(a) Record at publish:** do not record this as a consumer. Publication proves that an exact native snapshot exists; it does not prove that every subsequent fetch used it. Add a separate `published_exact` coverage state.
- **(b) N consecutive frames:** useful only as warm-up/hysteresis. It cannot make dropping safe when the route changes.
- **(c) Mixed downsample-chain fetches:** entirely plausible. Exact canonical keys and explicit fallback reasons will expose this.

### Robust design

Track the full normalized `TextureCache::TextureKey`, or a public equivalent `ResolveDestKey`, rather than `dest_base`. The existing key contains the relevant base, shape, pitch, mip, format, tiling, endian, signedness and scaled-resolve identity in [texture_cache.h:125](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/texture_cache.h:125>).

For each exact key and generation, record:

```text
published_exact
native_served
lle_fallback(reason)
present_native / present_fallback
```

Every covered fetch must finish classification with either `native_served` or `lle_fallback`; no silent early exit. Change the persistent edge structure to:

```text
src_rt_key -> set/vector of exact resolve destinations
```

Drop a transfer only if every affected logical destination is exactly published and every observed consumer was native.

The fully general fail-closed solution is lazy materialization: retain a pending LLE-transfer obligation and execute it immediately before the first actual LLE consumer. A previous-frame census is always a prediction and cannot guarantee that the next frame wonƒ?Tt take a new path. For BD, the exact-key census can be a practical first implementation, but publication alone must never authorize the drop.

## 2. `copy_dest_exp_bias`

It is part of the resolve operation, not the later texture consumer.

`RB_COPY_DEST_INFO.copy_dest_exp_bias` is defined separately from draw-output `RB_COLOR_INFO.color_exp_bias` in [registers.h:870](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/registers.h:870>). `GetResolveInfo` reads it into the resolve description in [draw_util.cc:1194](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/draw_util.cc:1194>).

The decisive code paths are:

- A bitwise/fast resolve is selected only when bias is zero in [draw_util.cc:1279](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/draw_util.cc:1279>).
- The resolve shader decodes it as `2^copy_dest_exp_bias` in [resolve.xesli:128](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/shaders/resolve.xesli:128>).
- MSAA averaging, bias multiplication and R/B swapping occur in the resolve shader around [resolve.xesli:583](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/shaders/resolve.xesli:583>).
- A2B10 packing is defined in [pixel_formats.xesli:118](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/shaders/pixel_formats.xesli:118>).

For the BD field:

```text
resolved = average(sample0..sample3) * 2^-2
         = (sample0 + sample1 + sample2 + sample3) / 16
```

Then apply `copy_dest_swap`, then A2B10 UNORM packing.

Do not additionally apply `RB_COLOR_INFO.color_exp_bias`; that is the render-target export bias already handled while producing P. If the conversion shader bakes the swap, disable the current swapped sampled-view workaround for that T or you will swap twice.

## 3. Shader integration

```text
1 sample
```

Reuse the transfer passthrough vertex shader/fullscreen triangle infrastructure exposed around [vulkan_render_target_cache.h:1194](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.h:1194>), but give this pass its own pipeline layout and push-constant range.

The fragment shader should:

1. Fetch the selected sample or samples.
2. Apply Xenos averaging.
3. Multiply by `2^copy_dest_exp_bias`.
4. Apply R/B swap.
5. Quantize using the same XePack UNORM semantics.
6. Output to the A2B10 attachment, letting the ROP store the packed format.

For the initial BD slice, support 1x and 4x `k0123` average. Fail closed for other sample-select modes until implemented; then add `k0ƒ?İk3`, `k01`, and `k23`.

### Hook location

- the correct resolve generation.

Required synchronization is conventional:

```text
P: producer layout -> SHADER_READ_ONLY, FRAGMENT_SHADER read

draw

```

Initially leave the LLE resolve enabled and use the native T only for sampling. Once screenshots/logs prove exact parity, let the strengthened drop gate remove the redundant ownership transfer.

## 2. `copy_dest_exp_bias`

It is part of the resolve operation, not the later texture consumer.

`RB_COPY_DEST_INFO.copy_dest_exp_bias` is defined separately from draw-output `RB_COLOR_INFO.color_exp_bias` in [registers.h:870](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/registers.h:870>). `GetResolveInfo` reads it into the resolve description in [draw_util.cc:1194](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/draw_util.cc:1194>).

The decisive code paths are:

- A bitwise/fast resolve is selected only when bias is zero in [draw_util.cc:1279](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/draw_util.cc:1279>).
- The resolve shader decodes it as `2^copy_dest_exp_bias` in [resolve.xesli:128](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/shaders/resolve.xesli:128>).
- MSAA averaging, bias multiplication and R/B swapping occur in the resolve shader around [resolve.xesli:583](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/shaders/resolve.xesli:583>).
- A2B10 packing is defined in [pixel_formats.xesli:118](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/shaders/pixel_formats.xesli:118>).

For the BD field:

```text
resolved = average(sample0..sample3) * 2^-2
         = (sample0 + sample1 + sample2 + sample3) / 16
```

Then apply `copy_dest_swap`, then A2B10 UNORM packing.

Do not additionally apply `RB_COLOR_INFO.color_exp_bias`; that is the render-target export bias already handled while producing P. If the conversion shader bakes the swap, disable the current swapped sampled-view workaround for that T or you will swap twice.

## 3. Shader integration

Choose **C**, implemented as a conventional offline-built `.ps.xesl`.

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| A: hand-authored SPIR-V | Reject; brittle and difficult to validate |
| B: programmatic `spv::Builder` | Works, but far more code than this pass warrants |
| C: fullscreen fragment conversion | Recommended |
| D: compute `.cs.xesl` | Only after proving A2B10 storage-image support |

Xenia already uses a graphics path for gamma conversion because storage-image support for `VK_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32` is optional, documented directly in [vulkan_command_processor.cc:1468](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:1468>). A2B10 as a color attachment is the safer Turnip path.

### Concrete wiring

Add two fragment modules because the SPIR-V image type is static:

```text
bd_native_resolve_convert_1x.ps.xesl
bd_native_resolve_convert_ms.ps.xesl
```

Build them through the existing XESL shader-generation flow.

Descriptor layout:

```text
set 0, binding 0: VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_SAMPLED_IMAGE
```

No sampler is needed; use `texelFetch`.

Push constants:

```text
source origin / destination extent
copy_sample_select
copy_dest_exp_bias or precomputed ldexp(1.0f, bias)
copy_dest_swap
```

Destination T:

```text
VK_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32
VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT
VK_IMAGE_USAGE_SAMPLED_BIT
1 sample
```

Reuse the transfer passthrough vertex shader/fullscreen triangle infrastructure exposed around [vulkan_render_target_cache.h:1194](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.h:1194>), but give this pass its own pipeline layout and push-constant range.

The fragment shader should:

1. Fetch the selected sample or samples.
2. Apply Xenos averaging.
3. Multiply by `2^copy_dest_exp_bias`.
4. Apply R/B swap.
5. Quantize using the same XePack UNORM semantics.
6. Output to the A2B10 attachment, letting the ROP store the packed format.

For the initial BD slice, support 1x and 4x `k0123` average. Fail closed for other sample-select modes until implemented; then add `k0ƒ?İk3`, `k01`, and `k23`.

### Hook location

Hook inside `VulkanRenderTargetCache::Resolve()` immediately after successful `GetResolveInfo` and empty-rectangle validation around [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:1523](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:1523>), before the normal LLE copy work.

That location already has:

- resolved source RT identity;
- destination copy registers;
- sample selection;
- bias, swap and valid rectangle;
- the correct resolve generation.

Look up the current-epoch producer P by `src_rt_key`, convert into T keyed by the canonical destination resource key, then publish the alias only after recording the conversion pass. Move the current sideband publication out of `IssueCopy`, which currently happens around [vulkan_command_processor.cc:8763](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:8763>).

Required synchronization is conventional:

```text
P: producer layout -> SHADER_READ_ONLY, FRAGMENT_SHADER read
T: previous sampled state -> COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, color write
draw
T: color write -> SHADER_READ_ONLY, FRAGMENT_SHADER read
```

Initially leave the LLE resolve enabled and use the native T only for sampling. Once screenshots/logs prove exact parity, let the strengthened drop gate remove the redundant ownership transfer.

## 1. Drop reliability

The current counter is counted before `BdL5DropSafe` clears transfer vectors. `AddRenderTargetTransferStats` sees the requested transfers around [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6526](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6526>), while the L5 filtering and `clear()` happen later around [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6566](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:6566>).

Therefore:

```text
rt_transfers = transfers requested before filtering
```

It is not:

```text
rt_transfers = transfers actually executed
```

In the current [brick1_l9trace.log](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/scratch/blue-dragon/brick1_l9trace.log>), the `35` values occur in the earlier workload; the steady field is predominantly `45`. The native-consumer records for the five observed field/bloom destinations are themselves stable. That does not prove the transfers dropped, because the counter cannot answer that question.

Instrument these three numbers first:

```text
rt_transfers_requested
l5_transfer_entries_dropped
rt_transfers_executed
```

Increment `dropped` immediately before clearing the vector, and calculate `executed` after all filtering. Also log:

```text
dest canonical key
generation
requested entries
previous consumer bits
drop verdict
failure reason
```

### Why the existing census is still unsafe

Even if the missing-entry premise disappears, the current gate is not fully fail-closed:

- The native bit is recorded only after every redirect check succeeds in [vulkan_command_processor.cc:11354](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:11354>). Signedness, epoch, format, missing image, or swizzled-view failures exit without recording anything.
- In pure LLE, those fallback exits do not consistently set `kNonNative`; the relevant fallback marking is associated with the inactive native-renderer branch.
- `dest_base` is not a resource identity. Different dimensions, pitches, formats, mips, tiled state, or generations may reuse it.
- `persistent_resolve_edges_[src_rt_key] = edge` stores only one destination. BD can resolve one source RT to multiple bloom destinations, so the later edge overwrites the earlier one.
- A downsample chain can genuinely be mixed: one exact fetch may redirect, while another fetch of the same base with a different shape/mip/format falls back to LLE.

The decision on your options is:

- **(a) Record at publish:** do not record this as a consumer. Publication proves that an exact native snapshot exists; it does not prove that every subsequent fetch used it. Add a separate `published_exact` coverage state.
- **(b) N consecutive frames:** useful only as warm-up/hysteresis. It cannot make dropping safe when the route changes.
- **(c) Mixed downsample-chain fetches:** entirely plausible. Exact canonical keys and explicit fallback reasons will expose this.

### Robust design

Track the full normalized `TextureCache::TextureKey`, or a public equivalent `ResolveDestKey`, rather than `dest_base`. The existing key contains the relevant base, shape, pitch, mip, format, tiling, endian, signedness and scaled-resolve identity in [texture_cache.h:125](</C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New project 8/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/texture_cache.h:125>).

For each exact key and generation, record:

```text
published_exact
native_served
lle_fallback(reason)
present_native / present_fallback
```

Every covered fetch must finish classification with either `native_served` or `lle_fallback`; no silent early exit. Change the persistent edge structure to:

```text
src_rt_key -> set/vector of exact resolve destinations
```

Drop a transfer only if every affected logical destination is exactly published and every observed consumer was native.

The fully general fail-closed solution is lazy materialization: retain a pending LLE-transfer obligation and execute it immediately before the first actual LLE consumer. A previous-frame census is always a prediction and cannot guarantee that the next frame wonƒ?Tt take a new path. For BD, the exact-key census can be a practical first implementation, but publication alone must never authorize the drop.

For the initial BD slice, support 1x and 4x `k0123` average. Fail closed for other sample-select modes until implemented; then add `k0ƒ?İk3`, `k01`, and `k23`.

### Hook location

- destination copy registers;
- sample selection;
- bias, swap and valid rectangle;
- the correct resolve generation.

Required synchronization is conventional:

```text
P: producer layout -> SHADER_READ_ONLY, FRAGMENT_SHADER read
T: previous sampled state -> COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, color write

T: color write -> SHADER_READ_ONLY, FRAGMENT_SHADER read
```

Initially leave the LLE resolve enabled and use the native T only for sampling. Once screenshots/logs prove exact parity, let the strengthened drop gate remove the redundant ownership transfer.

## Build order

Build this in order:

1. Fix the counters and log exact drop verdicts.
2. Strengthen bloom coverage to canonical-key native/fallback classification.
3. Verify desktop correctness and actual executed-transfer reduction.
4. Thor A/B with captured evidence.
5. Add the MSAA+bias graphics converter.

Bloom reliability is the faster, lower-risk win because conversion already works. But the existing `rt_transfers` number cannot establish that ten transfers are intermittently surviving. If the corrected executed counter shows bloom is already dropping every field frame, skip further bloom work and move directly to the MSAA field converter. The field converter is the larger strategic unlock; only Thor fence measurements can establish its performance value.

  1138:       it = it_pre;
  1139:     }

  1147:   // reused by a different render target for the same tile): same color/depth

  1154:   }

  1156:     return nullptr;
  1157:   }

  1159:     return nullptr;
  1160:   }

  1167:     return nullptr;
  1168:   }

   678:           pitch_pixels_tile_aligned_scaled, max_render_target_width);
   679:       return false;
   680:     }
   681:   }
   682: 
   683:   // Get used render targets.
   684:   // [0] is depth / stencil where relevant, [1...4] is color.
   685:   // Depth / stencil testing / writing is before color in the pipeline.
   686:   uint32_t depth_and_color_rts_used_bits = 0;
   687:   // depth_and_color_rts_used_bits -> EDRAM base.
   688:   uint32_t edram_bases[1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets];
   689:   uint32_t resource_formats[1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets];
   690:   uint32_t rts_are_64bpp = 0;
   691:   if (is_rasterization_done) {
   692:     if (normalized_depth_control.z_enable ||
   693:         normalized_depth_control.stencil_enable) {
   694:       depth_and_color_rts_used_bits |= 1;
   695:       auto rb_depth_info = regs.Get<reg::RB_DEPTH_INFO>();
   696:       edram_bases[0] = rb_depth_info.depth_base;
   697:       // With pixel shader interlock, always the same addressing disregarding
   698:       // the format.
   699:       resource_formats[0] =
   700:           interlock_barrier_only ? 0 : uint32_t(rb_depth_info.depth_format);
   701:     }
   702:     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets; ++i) {
   703:       if (!(normalized_color_mask & (uint32_t(0b1111) << (4 * i)))) {
   704:         continue;
   705:       }
   706:       auto color_info = regs.Get<reg::RB_COLOR_INFO>(
   707:           reg::RB_COLOR_INFO::rt_register_indices[i]);
   708:       uint32_t rt_bit_index = 1 + i;
   709:       depth_and_color_rts_used_bits |= uint32_t(1) << rt_bit_index;
   710:       edram_bases[rt_bit_index] = color_info.color_base;
   711:       xenos::ColorRenderTargetFormat color_format =
   712:           regs.Get<reg::RB_COLOR_INFO>(
   713:                   reg::RB_COLOR_INFO::rt_register_indices[i])
   714:               .color_format;
   715:       bool is_64bpp = xenos::IsColorRenderTargetFormat64bpp(color_format);
   716:       if (is_64bpp) {
   717:         rts_are_64bpp |= uint32_t(1) << rt_bit_index;
   718:       }
   719:       xenos::ColorRenderTargetFormat color_resource_format;
   720:       if (interlock_barrier_only) {
   721:         // Only changes in mapping between coordinates and addresses are
   722:         // interesting (along with access overlap between draw calls), thus only
   723:         // pixel size is relevant.
   724:         color_resource_format =
   725:             is_64bpp ? xenos::ColorRenderTargetFormat::k_16_16_16_16
   726:                      : xenos::ColorRenderTargetFormat::k_8_8_8_8;
   727:       } else {
   728:         color_resource_format =
   729:             GetColorResourceFormat(xenos::GetStorageColorFormat(color_format));
   730:       }
   731:       resource_formats[rt_bit_index] = uint32_t(color_resource_format);
   732:     }
   733:   }
   734: 
   735:   uint32_t rts_remaining;
   736:   uint32_t rt_index;
   737: 
   738:   // Eliminate other bound render targets if their EDRAM base conflicts with
   739:   // another render target - it's an error in most host implementations to bind
   740:   // the same render target into multiple slots, also the behavior would be
   741:   // unpredictable if that happens.
   742:   // Depth is considered the least important as it's earlier in the pipeline
   743:   // (issues caused by color and depth render target collisions haven't been
   744:   // found yet), but render targets with smaller index are considered more
   745:   // important - specifically, because of the usage in the lighting pass of
   746:   // 4D5307E6, which can be checked in the vertical look calibration sequence in
   747:   // the beginning of the game: if render target 0 is removed in favor of 1, the
   748:   // characters and the world will be too dark, like fully in shadow -
   749:   // especially prominent on the helmet. This happens because the shader picks
   750:   // between two render targets to write dynamically (though with a static, bool
   751:   // constant condition), but all other state is set up in a way that implies
   752:   // the same render target being bound twice. On Direct3D 9, if you don't write
   753:   // to a color pixel shader output on the control flow that was taken, the
   754:   // render target will not be written to. However, this has been relaxed in
   755:   // Direct3D 10, where if the shader declares an output, it's assumed to be
   756:   // always written (or with an undefined value otherwise).
   757:   rts_remaining = depth_and_color_rts_used_bits & ~(uint32_t(1));
   758:   while (xe::bit_scan_forward(rts_remaining, &rt_index)) {
   759:     rts_remaining &= ~(uint32_t(1) << rt_index);
   760:     uint32_t edram_base = edram_bases[rt_index];
   761:     uint32_t rts_other_remaining =
   762:         depth_and_color_rts_used_bits &
   763:         (~((uint32_t(1) << (rt_index + 1)) - 1) | uint32_t(1));
   764:     uint32_t rt_other_index;
   765:     while (xe::bit_scan_forward(rts_other_remaining, &rt_other_index)) {
   766:       rts_other_remaining &= ~(uint32_t(1) << rt_other_index);
   767:       if (edram_bases[rt_other_index] == edram_base) {
   768:         depth_and_color_rts_used_bits &= ~(uint32_t(1) << rt_other_index);
   769:       }
   770:     }
   771:   }
   772: 
   773:   // Clear ownership transfers before adding any.
   774:   if (!interlock_barrier_only) {
   775:     for (size_t i = 0; i < xe::countof(last_update_transfers_); ++i) {
   776:       last_update_transfers_[i].clear();
   777:     }
   778:   }
   779: 
   780:   if (!depth_and_color_rts_used_bits) {
   781:     // Nothing to bind, don't waste time on things like memexport-only draws -
   782:     // just check if old bindings can still be used.
   783:     std::memset(last_update_used_render_targets_, 0,
   784:                 sizeof(last_update_used_render_targets_));
   785:     if (are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_) {
   786:       for (size_t i = 0;
   787:            i < xe::countof(last_update_accumulated_render_targets_); ++i) {
   788:         const RenderTarget* render_target =
   789:             last_update_accumulated_render_targets_[i];
   790:         if (!render_target) {
   791:           continue;
   792:         }
   793:         RenderTargetKey rt_key = render_target->key();
   794:         if (rt_key.pitch_tiles_at_32bpp != pitch_tiles_at_32bpp ||
   795:             rt_key.msaa_samples != msaa_samples) {
   796:           are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_ = false;
   797:           break;
   798:         }
   799:       }
   800:     }
   801:     if (!are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_) {
   802:       std::memset(last_update_accumulated_render_targets_, 0,
   803:                   sizeof(last_update_accumulated_render_targets_));
   804:     }
   805:     return true;
   806:   }
   807: 
   808:   // Estimate height used by render targets (for color for writes, for depth /
   809:   // stencil for both reads and writes) from various sources.
   810:   uint32_t height_used = std::min(
   811:       GetRenderTargetHeight(pitch_tiles_at_32bpp, msaa_samples),
   812:       draw_extent_estimator_.EstimateMaxY(
   813:           interlock_barrier_only
   814:               ? cvars::execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu_for_psi_render_backend
   815:               : true,
   816:           vertex_shader));
   817:   // HLE BIN-ONCE: the single forced tile spans the FULL surface, but EstimateMaxY
   818:   // only sees the top tile's scissored extent (~672) so the bottom tile's geometry
   819:   // has no RT. Force the full-surface height (BD field = 1280) so the whole scene
   820:   // fits the one pass. Clamped to the pitch's real max to avoid ballooning.
   821:   if (cvars::gpu_binonce_full_scissor) {
   822:     height_used = std::min(
   823:         GetRenderTargetHeight(pitch_tiles_at_32bpp, msaa_samples), 1280u);
   824:   }
   825: 
   826:   // Sorted by EDRAM base and then by index in the pipeline - for simplicity,
   827:   // treat render targets placed closer to the end of the EDRAM as truncating
   828:   // the previous one (and in case multiple render targets are placed at the
   829:   // same EDRAM base, though normally this shouldn't happen, treat the color
   830:   // ones as more important than the depth one, which may be not needed and just
   831:   // a leftover if the draw, for instance, has depth / stencil happening to be
   832:   // always passing and never writing with the current state, and also because
   833:   // depth testing has to happen before the color is written). Overall it's
   834:   // normal for estimated EDRAM ranges of render targets to intersect if drawing
   835:   // without a viewport (as there's nothing to clamp the estimated height) and
   836:   // multiple render targets are bound.
   837:   std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>
   838:       edram_bases_sorted[1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets];
   839:   uint32_t edram_bases_sorted_count = 0;
   840:   rts_remaining = depth_and_color_rts_used_bits;
   841:   while (xe::bit_scan_forward(rts_remaining, &rt_index)) {
   842:     rts_remaining &= ~(uint32_t(1) << rt_index);
   843:     edram_bases_sorted[edram_bases_sorted_count++] =
   844:         std::make_pair(edram_bases[rt_index], rt_index);
   845:   }
   846:   std::sort(edram_bases_sorted, edram_bases_sorted + edram_bases_sorted_count);
   847:   // "As if it was 64bpp" (contribution of 32bpp render targets multiplied by 2,
   848:   // and clamping for 32bpp render targets divides this by 2) because 32bpp
   849:   // render targets can be combined with twice as long 64bpp render targets. An
   850:   // example is the 4541099D menu background (1-sample 1152x720, or 1200x720
   851:   // after rounding to tiles, with a 32bpp depth buffer at 0 requiring 675
   852:   // tiles, and a 64bpp color buffer at 675 requiring 1350 tiles, but the
   853:   // smallest distance between two render target bases is 675 tiles).
   854:   uint32_t rt_max_distance_tiles_at_64bpp = xenos::kEdramTileCount * 2;
   855:   if (cvars::mrt_edram_used_range_clamp_to_min &&
   856:       edram_bases_sorted_count >= 2) {
   857:     for (uint32_t i = 1; i < edram_bases_sorted_count; ++i) {
   858:       const std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>& rt_base_prev =
   859:           edram_bases_sorted[i - 1];
   860:       rt_max_distance_tiles_at_64bpp =
   861:           std::min(rt_max_distance_tiles_at_64bpp,
   862:                    (edram_bases_sorted[i].first - rt_base_prev.first)
   863:                        << (((rts_are_64bpp >> rt_base_prev.second) & 1) ^ 1));
   864:     }
   865:     // Clamp to the distance from the last render target to the first with
   866:     // EDRAM addressing wrapping.
   867:     const std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>& rt_base_last =
   868:         edram_bases_sorted[edram_bases_sorted_count - 1];
   869:     rt_max_distance_tiles_at_64bpp =
   870:         std::min(rt_max_distance_tiles_at_64bpp,
   871:                  (xenos::kEdramTileCount + edram_bases_sorted[0].first -
   872:                   rt_base_last.first)
   873:                      << (((rts_are_64bpp >> rt_base_last.second) & 1) ^ 1));
   874:   }
   875: 
   876:   // Make sure all the needed render targets are created, and gather lengths of
   877:   // ranges used by each render target.
   878:   RenderTargetKey rt_keys[1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets];
   879:   RenderTarget* rts[1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets];
   880:   uint32_t rt_lengths_tiles[1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets];
   881:   // NOTE (BD-30 MSAA ghost, 2026-06-30): forcing a guest 2x surface to host 1x
   882:   // (gpu_force_max_msaa_samples) HALVES its EDRAM tile footprint - MSAA samples
   883:   // ARE tiles. BD packs a 2x main scene + 4x effect buffers into shared EDRAM
   884:   // bases, so the halved range lets the bright effect buffer bleed in (the
   885:   // "bright dupe of objects"). Reserving the range at the guest msaa here fixes
   886:   // the bleed but then OVER-CLAIMS into the next RT's tiles (clamped to
   887:   // rt_max_distance below) -> displaces the output RT -> letterbox. That was the
   888:   // per-site dead end (cap=1 "intrinsically not clean").
   889:   //
   890:   // BRICK 2 (gpu_native_render_targets): revisit the "reserve at guest msaa" fix
   891:   // but pair it with RENDER-TARGET INDEPENDENCE (cross-RT ownership transfers
   892:   // suppressed below). Reserving each RT's ownership footprint at the GUEST
   893:   // (pre-clamp) sample count makes the EDRAM ownership map match the guest layout
   894:   // so nothing bleeds; suppressing the cross-RT transfers stops the over-claim
   895:   // from physically displacing the shared-base 1x output RT (the letterbox
   896:   // vector) - the output keeps its own pixels. The host image/render pass/resolve
   897:   // stay at the clamped sample count (the ROP win). rb_surface_info.msaa_samples
   898:   // is the UNCLAMPED guest value (only the local msaa_samples was clamped above).
   899:   // Inert unless the cvar and a clamp are both active (then guest == clamped).
   900:   xenos::MsaaSamples ownership_msaa_samples =
   901:       cvars::gpu_native_render_targets ? rb_surface_info.msaa_samples
   902:                                        : msaa_samples;
   903:   uint32_t length_used_tiles_at_32bpp =
   904:       ((height_used
   905:         << uint32_t(ownership_msaa_samples >= xenos::MsaaSamples::k2X)) +
   906:        (xenos::kEdramTileHeightSamples - 1)) /
   907:       xenos::kEdramTileHeightSamples * pitch_tiles_at_32bpp;
   908:   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < edram_bases_sorted_count; ++i) {
   909:     const std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>& rt_base_index = edram_bases_sorted[i];
   910:     uint32_t rt_base = rt_base_index.first;
   911:     uint32_t rt_bit_index = rt_base_index.second;
   912:     RenderTargetKey& rt_key = rt_keys[rt_bit_index];
   913:     rt_key.base_tiles = rt_base;
   914:     rt_key.pitch_tiles_at_32bpp = pitch_tiles_at_32bpp;
   915:     rt_key.msaa_samples = msaa_samples;
   916:     rt_key.is_depth = rt_bit_index == 0;
   917:     rt_key.resource_format = resource_formats[rt_bit_index];
   918:     if (!interlock_barrier_only) {
   919:       RenderTarget* render_target = GetOrCreateRenderTarget(rt_key);
   920:       if (!render_target) {
   921:         return false;
   922:       }
   923:       rts[rt_bit_index] = render_target;
   924:     }
   925:     uint32_t rt_is_64bpp = (rts_are_64bpp >> rt_bit_index) & 1;
   926:     // The last render target can occupy the EDRAM until the base of the first
   927:     // render target (itself in case of 1 render target) with EDRAM addressing
   928:     // wrapping.
   929:     rt_lengths_tiles[i] = std::min(
   930:         std::min(length_used_tiles_at_32bpp << rt_is_64bpp,
   931:                  rt_max_distance_tiles_at_64bpp >> (rt_is_64bpp ^ 1)),
   932:         ((i + 1 < edram_bases_sorted_count)
   933:              ? edram_bases_sorted[i + 1].first
   934:              : (xenos::kEdramTileCount + edram_bases_sorted[0].first)) -
   935:             rt_base);
   936:   }
   937: 
   938:   if (interlock_barrier_only) {
   939:     // Because a full pixel shader interlock barrier may clear the ownership map
   940:     // (since it flushes all previous writes, and there's no need for another
   941:     // barrier if an overlap is encountered later between pre-barrier and
   942:     // post-barrier usages), check if any overlap requiring a barrier happens,
   943:     // and then insert the barrier if needed.
   944:     bool interlock_barrier_needed = false;
   945:     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < edram_bases_sorted_count; ++i) {
   946:       const std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>& rt_base_index =
   947:           edram_bases_sorted[i];
   948:       if (WouldOwnershipChangeRequireTransfers(rt_keys[rt_base_index.second], 0,
   949:                                                rt_lengths_tiles[i])) {
   950:         interlock_barrier_needed = true;
   951:         break;
   952:       }
   953:     }
   954:     if (interlock_barrier_needed) {
   955:       RequestPixelShaderInterlockBarrier();
   956:     }
   957:   }
   958: 
   959:   // From now on ownership transfers should succeed for simplicity and
   960:   // consistency, even if they fail in the implementation (just ignore that and
   961:   // draw with whatever contents currently are in the render target in this
   962:   // case).
   963: 
   964:   // BRICK 2 (gpu_native_render_targets): INDEPENDENT render targets. Still update
   965:   // ownership (so resolves + RT-as-texture find the correct owner), but do NOT
   966:   // record cross-RT transfer copies. With a force-clamped MSAA the shared-base 2x
   967:   // main scene and the 1x output/effect buffers would otherwise physically
   968:   // inherit each other's pixels through these transfers (the ghost/letterbox
   969:   // vector once their guest-shared EDRAM bases misalign after the clamp). BD's
   970:   // composites read the main scene via resolve->shared-memory->texture, not via
   971:   // these EDRAM ownership transfers, so suppressing the copies does not break the
   972:   // composite reads. Gated + default-off => byte-identical otherwise.
   973:   const bool native_rts_independent =
   974:       cvars::gpu_native_render_targets && !interlock_barrier_only;
   975:   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < edram_bases_sorted_count; ++i) {
   976:     const std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>& rt_base_index = edram_bases_sorted[i];
   977:     uint32_t rt_bit_index = rt_base_index.second;
   978:     ChangeOwnership(rt_keys[rt_bit_index], 0, rt_lengths_tiles[i],
   979:                     (interlock_barrier_only || native_rts_independent)
   980:                         ? nullptr
   981:                         : &last_update_transfers_[rt_bit_index]);
   982:   }
   983: 
   984:   if (interlock_barrier_only) {
   985:     // No copying transfers or render target bindings - only needed the barrier.
   986:     return true;
   987:   }
   988: 
   989:   // If everything succeeded, update the used render targets.
   990:   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets; ++i) {
   991:     last_update_used_render_targets_[i] =
   992:         (depth_and_color_rts_used_bits & (uint32_t(1) << i)) ? rts[i] : nullptr;
   993:   }
   994:   if (are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_) {
   995:     // Check if the only re-enabling a previously bound render target.
   996:     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets; ++i) {
   997:       RenderTarget* current_rt =
   998:           (depth_and_color_rts_used_bits & (uint32_t(1) << i)) ? rts[i]
   999:                                                                : nullptr;
  1000:       const RenderTarget* accumulated_rt =
  1001:           last_update_accumulated_render_targets_[i];
  1002:       if (!accumulated_rt) {
  1003:         if (current_rt) {
  1004:           // Binding a totally new render target - won't keep the existing
  1005:           // render pass anyway, no much need to try to re-enable previously
  1006:           // disabled render targets in other slots as well, even though that
  1007:           // would be valid.
  1008:           are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_ = false;
  1009:           break;
  1010:         }
  1011:         // Append the new render target.
  1012:         last_update_accumulated_render_targets_[i] = current_rt;
  1013:         continue;
  1014:       }
  1015:       if (current_rt) {
  1016:         if (current_rt != accumulated_rt) {
  1017:           // Changing a render target in a slot.
  1018:           are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_ = false;
  1019:           break;
  1020:         }
  1021:       } else {
  1022:         RenderTargetKey accumulated_rt_key = accumulated_rt->key();
  1023:         if (accumulated_rt_key.pitch_tiles_at_32bpp != pitch_tiles_at_32bpp ||
  1024:             accumulated_rt_key.msaa_samples != msaa_samples) {
  1025:           // The previously bound render target is incompatible with the
  1026:           // current surface info.
  1027:           are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_ = false;
  1028:           break;
  1029:         }
  1030:       }
  1031:     }
  1032:     // Make sure the same render target isn't bound into two different slots
  1033:     // over time.
  1034:     for (uint32_t i = 1; are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_ &&
  1035:                          i < 1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets;
  1036:          ++i) {
  1037:       const RenderTarget* render_target =
  1038:           last_update_accumulated_render_targets_[i];
  1039:       if (!render_target) {
  1040:         continue;
  1041:       }
  1042:       for (uint32_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) {
  1043:         if (last_update_accumulated_render_targets_[j] == render_target) {
  1044:           are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_ = false;
  1045:           break;
  1046:         }
  1047:       }
  1048:     }
  1049:   }
  1050:   if (!are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_) {
  1051:     std::memcpy(last_update_accumulated_render_targets_,
  1052:                 last_update_used_render_targets_,
  1053:                 sizeof(last_update_accumulated_render_targets_));
  1054:     are_accumulated_render_targets_valid_ = true;
  1055:   }
  1056: 
  1057:   return true;
  1058: }
  1059: 
  1060: uint32_t RenderTargetCache::GetLastUpdateBoundRenderTargets(
  1061:     uint32_t* depth_and_color_formats_out) const {
  1062:   if (GetPath() != Path::kHostRenderTargets) {
  1063:     if (depth_and_color_formats_out) {
  1064:       std::memset(depth_and_color_formats_out, 0,
  1065:                   sizeof(uint32_t) * (1 + xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets));

docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-37-BD's field renders ~42 render passes, most breaking because post-process **composites read a
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md:38:producer RT from an EARLIER pass at a TRANSFORMED texcoord** (not same-pixel). On the Adreno 740
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-39-TBDR each such break evicts GMEM to DRAM + reloads (the ~74ms tile-I/O, device-isolated via
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-40-`gpu_edram_passes_dont_care` 128->49ms). Desktop immediate-mode GPUs ("fable") pay none of this —
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-41-they read the producer from VRAM directly. That architectural gap is the whole difficulty.
