docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-529-  Worked the tile-I/O accounting through precisely. Hardware fact: on a TBDR (Adreno/Turnip) a COMPUTE
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-530-  dispatch does NOT use the tiling/GMEM/binning path — it reads/writes DRAM images & buffers directly (this
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-531-  is why xenia's EDRAM resolves are already compute dispatches). Therefore for a composite consumer C (reads
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-532-  producer P as texture tf0, writes dest D):
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md:533:  - As a FRAGMENT draw in its own render pass: (1) P must be stored to DRAM to be sampled = the brk_img_sr
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-534-    (P ATTACHMENT->SHADER_READ); (2) C's render pass LOADS D's tiles, renders, STORES D's tiles.
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-535-  - As a COMPUTE dispatch: (1) P still stored (unchanged); (2) compute samples P and writes D straight to a
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-536-    DRAM storage image — **NO render-pass tile load/store for D at all.**
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-537-  - So converting C to compute REMOVES D's tile load+store (~a tile-resolve's worth), and for a CHAIN
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-538-    (blur pyramid P->C1->C2->C3: the 13-tap 1B13 + friends) it removes ALL the intermediate stores+loads —
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md-539-    each Di is compute-written to DRAM and compute-read by the next, zero render-pass tile-I/O across the chain.
docs\research\20260701-bd30-edram-lever-synthesis.md:540:    The initial P store stays (that's the residual brk_img_sr; removing it needs the producer-SSBO buffer path).

   36: ## The problem, precisely
   37: BD's field renders ~42 render passes, most breaking because post-process **composites read a
   38: producer RT from an EARLIER pass at a TRANSFORMED texcoord** (not same-pixel). On the Adreno 740
   39: TBDR each such break evicts GMEM to DRAM + reloads (the ~74ms tile-I/O, device-isolated via
   40: `gpu_edram_passes_dont_care` 128->49ms). Desktop immediate-mode GPUs ("fable") pay none of this Г?"
   41: they read the producer from VRAM directly. That architectural gap is the whole difficulty.
   42:

  385:     // May be zero if the original rectangle was somehow specified in a
  386:     // totally broken way - in this case, the resolve must be dropped.
  387:     uint32_t width_div_8 : xenos::kResolveSizeBits -
  388:                            xenos::kResolveAlignmentPixelsLog2;
  389: 
  390:     // 1 to 7.
  391:     uint32_t draw_resolution_scale_x : 3;
  392:     uint32_t draw_resolution_scale_y : 3;
  393:   };

  396:   }
  397: };

  481: struct ResolveInfo {
  482:   reg::RB_COPY_CONTROL rb_copy_control;
  483: 
  484:   // depth_edram_info / depth_original_base and color_edram_info /
  485:   // color_original_base are set up if copying or clearing color and depth
  486:   // respectively, according to RB_COPY_CONTROL.
  487:   ResolveEdramInfo depth_edram_info;
  488:   ResolveEdramInfo color_edram_info;
  489:   // Original bases, without adjustment to a 160x32 region for packed offsets,
  490:   // for locating host render targets to perform clears if host render targets
  491:   // are used for EDRAM emulation - the same as the base that the render target
  492:   // will likely be used for drawing next, to prevent unneeded tile ownership
  493:   // transfers between clears and first usage if clearing a subregion.
  494:   uint32_t depth_original_base;
  495:   uint32_t color_original_base;
  496: 
  497:   ResolveCoordinateInfo coordinate_info;
  498:   // Like coordinate_info.width_div_8, but not needed for shaders.
  499:   // In pixels.
  500:   // May be zero if the original rectangle was somehow specified in a totally
  501:   // broken way - in this case, the resolve must be dropped.
  502:   uint32_t height_div_8;
  503: 
  504:   reg::RB_COPY_DEST_INFO copy_dest_info;
  505:   ResolveCopyDestCoordinateInfo copy_dest_coordinate_info;
  506: 
  507:   // The address of the texture or the location within the texture that
  508:   // copy_dest_coordinate_info.offset_x/y_div_8 - the origin of the copy
  509:   // destination - is relative to.
  510:   uint32_t copy_dest_base;
  511:   // Memory range that will potentially be modified by copying to the texture.
  512:   // copy_dest_extent_length may be zero if something is wrong with the
  513:   // destination, in this case, clearing may still be done, but copying must be
  514:   // dropped.
  515:   uint32_t copy_dest_extent_start;
  516:   uint32_t copy_dest_extent_length;
  517: 
  518:   // The clear shaders always write to a uint4 view of EDRAM.
  519:   uint32_t rb_depth_clear;
  520:   uint32_t rb_color_clear;
  521:   uint32_t rb_color_clear_lo;
  522: 
  523:   bool IsCopyingDepth() const {
  524:     return rb_copy_control.copy_src_select >= xenos::kMaxColorRenderTargets;
  525:   }
  526: 
  527:   // See GetResolveEdramTileSpan documentation for explanation.
  528:   void GetCopyEdramTileSpan(uint32_t& base_out, uint32_t& row_length_used_out,
  529:                             uint32_t& rows_out, uint32_t& pitch_out) const {
  530:     ResolveEdramInfo edram_info =
  531:         IsCopyingDepth() ? depth_edram_info : color_edram_info;
  532:     GetResolveEdramTileSpan(edram_info, coordinate_info, height_div_8, base_out,
  533:                             row_length_used_out, rows_out);
  534:     pitch_out = edram_info.pitch_tiles;
  535:   }

  752: VkFormat VulkanTextureCache::GetHostVkFormatForColorFormat(
  753:     xenos::TextureFormat texture_format) const {
  754:   // The resolve dest ColorFormat is reinterpreted as a TextureFormat (see
  755:   // draw_util GetResolveInfo). Map it to the same host VkFormat a sampled
  756:   // texture of that format uses. Direct host_formats_ index is correct for the
  757:   // non-YUV color formats BD resolves to (k_2_10_10_10, k_8_8_8_8, etc.); the
  758:   // YUV special cases in GetHostFormatPair need a width and never appear as a
  759:   // resolve dest here.
  760:   uint32_t index = uint32_t(texture_format);
  761:   if (index >= xe::countof(host_formats_)) {
  762:     return VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED;
  763:   }
  764:   return host_formats_[index].format_unsigned.format;
  765: }

   35: // THE real-HLE unit (EDRAM deletion): a single native render-to-texture surface
   36: // ƒ?" its OWN persistent color(+depth) VkImage, keyed by the guest RESOLVE-
   37: // DESTINATION address (the stable D3D9 resource identity: the main-memory
   38: // texture the 360 surface resolves to and is LATER SAMPLED as). Because each
   39: // logical surface owns one image that is BOTH rendered into AND sampled, there
   40: // are NO EDRAM ownership transfers (the 35-pass / ~110ms wall). This replaces
   41: // xenia's EDRAM-base RenderTargetKey addressing with DXVK/Cemu-style
   42: // resource-identity addressing. Single-sample first (shadow/reflection RTs);
   43: // MSAA aux resolve is a follow-up.
   44: struct NativeSurface {
   45:   uint32_t key = 0;  // resolve-dest guest address = resource identity
   46:   uint32_t width = 0;
   47:   uint32_t height = 0;
   48:   VkFormat color_format = VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED;
   49:   VkFormat depth_format = VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED;
   50:   VkSampleCountFlagBits samples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT;
   51:   VkImage color_image = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
   52:   VkDeviceMemory color_memory = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
   53:   VkImageView color_view = VK_NULL_HANDLE;  // SAMPLED + COLOR_ATTACHMENT
   54:   VkImage depth_image = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
   55:   VkDeviceMemory depth_memory = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
   56:   VkImageView depth_view = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
   57:   VkRenderPass render_pass_clear = VK_NULL_HANDLE;  // first draw into this surface
   58:   VkRenderPass render_pass_load = VK_NULL_HANDLE;   // accumulate re-begins
   59:   VkFramebuffer framebuffer = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
   60:   // Tracks the color image's current layout so binds/attaches barrier correctly.
   61:   VkImageLayout color_layout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
   62:   bool rendered_this_frame = false;  // false => next attach uses the CLEAR pass
   63: };
   64: 
   65: // Brick 1: owns a persistent native full-surface color+depth RT + one render
   66: // pass. Bricks 2-4 add native pipelines (VkBuffer vertex-input, Xenos->SPIR-V,
   67: // hardware ROP blend), the captured-draw submit loop, depth-prepass + early-Z,
   68: // and composite folding. Kept deliberately separate from RenderTargetCache so it
   69: // does NOT go through the EDRAM tile/transfer/resolve machinery.
   70: class BdNativeRenderer {
   71:  public:
   72:   explicit BdNativeRenderer(VulkanCommandProcessor& command_processor)
   73:       : command_processor_(command_processor) {}
   74:   ~BdNativeRenderer() { Shutdown(); }
   75: 
   76:   // Allocate the persistent color+depth image + render pass + framebuffer, sized
   77:   // to BD's full field surface (default 720x1280; the real dims come from the
   78:   // captured surface state). Returns false on failure (caller falls back to LLE).
   79:   // stretch_src_width: when >0, the field renders into the left stretch_src_width
   80:   // px and is blitted STRETCHED to the full width on present (fill the screen);
   81:   // 0 = present the rendered region as-is.
   82:   bool Initialize(uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t stretch_src_width = 0);
   83:   void Shutdown();
   84: 
   85:   // Recreate the color image + view + render pass + framebuffer for `format` if
   86:   // it differs from the current one - so xenia's field pipelines (built for the
   87:   // field's color format) are render-pass-COMPATIBLE with the native pass (else
   88:   // "device lost"). Call BEFORE redirecting a field draw (pass not yet begun, so
   89:   // the images aren't in use). Returns false on failure.
   90:   bool EnsureColorFormat(VkFormat color_format, VkFormat depth_format,
   91:                          VkSampleCountFlagBits samples);
   92: 
   93:   // Brick 2a: begin the ONE held-open native render pass on `command_buffer`
   94:   // (clears color+depth), then EndRenderPass. Bricks 2b-3 record the captured
   95:   // 0x82489F40 draws (native pipelines + vertex-input) BETWEEN begin and end.
   96:   // Leaves color_image_ in SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL (finalLayout) for present.
   97:   // Uses xenia's DeferredCommandBuffer (recorded on the CP thread, replayed on
   98:   // the worker) - NOT a raw VkCommandBuffer - so it slots into the frame flow.
   99:   void RenderFrame(DeferredCommandBuffer& command_buffer);
  100: 
  101:   bool initialized() const { return render_pass_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE; }
  102:   VkImage color_image() const { return color_image_; }
  103:   // Sampled color view to present. When the field is MSAA (samples_ > 1) the
  104:   // render pass resolves color into a SINGLE-SAMPLE resolve image - present THAT
  105:   // (an MSAA image sampled directly bands). Single-sample: present color directly.
  106:   VkImageView color_view() const {
  107:     return (samples_ != VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT && resolve_view_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE)
  108:                ? resolve_view_
  109:                : color_view_;
  110:   }
  111:   // The view to PRESENT: the stretched present image when stretch is active + ready,
  112:   // else the rendered image directly (color_view()).
  113:   VkImageView present_output_view() const {
  114:     if (stretch_src_width_ > 0 && present_view_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE &&
  115:         present_image_ready_) {
  116:       return present_view_;
  117:     }
  118:     return color_view();
  119:   }
  120:   // The single-sample image holding the rendered field (resolve when MSAA, else
  121:   // color) - the SOURCE for the stretch blit.
  122:   VkImage rendered_image() const {
  123:     return (samples_ != VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT && resolve_image_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE)
  124:                ? resolve_image_
  125:                : color_image_;
  126:   }
  127:   // BD field-fill STRETCH: the bin-once renders the whole field into the left
  128:   // src_width px of the native RT (the field's guest surface is narrower than the
  129:   // 1280 display - BD upscales it in the resolve). Blit that region to the full
  130:   // present_image_ width so the field fills the screen, then present present_image_.
  131:   // No-op (returns false) if the present image isn't allocated (stretch disabled).
  132:   bool StretchToPresent(DeferredCommandBuffer& command_buffer, uint32_t src_width,
  133:                         uint32_t src_height);
  134:   // ADRENO: the render pass has no in-pass resolve (for pipeline compat), so resolve
  135:   // the MSAA color -> single-sample resolve_image_ SEPARATELY before present. No-op
  136:   // on desktop (in-pass resolve) or single-sample. Call before present/StretchToPresent.
  137:   bool ResolveMsaa(DeferredCommandBuffer& command_buffer);
  138:   bool has_present_image() const { return present_image_ != VK_NULL_HANDLE; }
  139:   // The native render pass + framebuffer - redirect BD's field draws into these
  140:   // to render the real geometry natively in ONE pass (Brick 2b, reuses xenia's
  141:   // shaders/pipelines; requires format-compatibility with the field pipelines).
  142:   VkFramebuffer framebuffer() const { return framebuffer_; }
  143:   // Two render passes (both compatible with framebuffer_): the CLEAR pass for the
  144:   // FIRST redirected field draw of a frame, the LOAD pass (preserves content,
  145:   // initial+final layout SHADER_READ) for every re-begin - so geometry ACCUMULATES
  146:   // across mid-frame pass breaks instead of being wiped (the black-render fix).
  147:   VkRenderPass render_pass_load() const { return render_pass_load_; }
  148:   VkRenderPass render_pass() const { return render_pass_; }
  149:   uint32_t width() const { return width_; }
  150:   uint32_t height() const { return height_; }
  151:   // THE desktop-vs-Thor fork: true on Qualcomm Adreno / Mesa Turnip (the driver
  152:   // that crashes on the loose render-pass compat desktop tolerates). Branch
  153:   // Adreno-strict / super-optimized paths on this.
  154:   bool IsAdreno() const;
  155: 
  156:   // ---- Native-surface registry (the real HLE / EDRAM-deletion substrate) ----
  157:   // Get-or-create the persistent native surface for resource `key` (the guest
  158:   // resolve-destination address), sized/typed to the surface. Reused across
  159:   // frames; recreated in place if the format/size/samples change. Returns nullptr
  160:   // on failure (caller falls back to the EDRAM path). MSAA (samples>1) is not yet
  161:   // supported for aux surfaces and returns nullptr.
  162:   NativeSurface* AcquireSurface(uint32_t key, uint32_t width, uint32_t height,
  163:                                 VkFormat color_format, VkFormat depth_format,
  164:                                 VkSampleCountFlagBits samples);
  165:   // Look up a native surface by key (nullptr if none). Const view for binding.
  166:   NativeSurface* FindSurface(uint32_t key);
  167:   // The sampled color view of the native surface whose key == guest_address, or
  168:   // VK_NULL_HANDLE if none exists ƒ?" the texture-fetch redirect uses this to bind
  169:   // the natively-rendered image instead of the EDRAM-resolved upload. Only
  170:   // returns a view once the surface has actually been rendered this run (else the
  171:   // image is undefined/garbage and must fall back to EDRAM).
  172:   VkImageView LookupSampledSurface(uint32_t guest_address);
  173:   // Number of live native surfaces (diagnostics).
  174:   size_t surface_count() const { return surfaces_.size(); }
  175:   // Clear per-frame render flags on all surfaces (call at frame start): the next
  176:   // draw into each surface re-CLEARs it, matching BD re-priming its RTs per frame.
  177:   void BeginSurfaceFrame();
  178: 
  179:  private:
  180:   bool CreateRenderPass();
  181:   bool CreateImages();
  182:   bool CreateFramebuffer();
  183:   // Allocate images/views/passes/framebuffer into `surface` per its fields.
  184:   bool CreateSurfaceResources(NativeSurface& surface);
  185:   void DestroySurfaceResources(NativeSurface& surface);
  186: 
  187:   // key(resolve-dest guest address) -> persistent native surface. Node stability
  188:   // (unordered_map) so returned NativeSurface* stay valid across inserts.
  189:   std::unordered_map<uint32_t, NativeSurface> surfaces_;
  190: 
  191:   VulkanCommandProcessor& command_processor_;
  192:   uint32_t width_ = 0;
  193:   uint32_t height_ = 0;
  194: 
  195:   // Native (NON-EDRAM) attachments ƒ?" the whole point: no tile/transfer machinery.
  196:   VkImage color_image_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  197:   VkDeviceMemory color_memory_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  198:   VkImageView color_view_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  199:   // Single-sample resolve target (only when samples_ > 1) - the MSAA color

  209:   VkImageView present_view_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;

 4293: 
 4294: void VulkanCommandProcessor::SubmitBarriersAndEnterRenderTargetCacheRenderPass(
 4295:     VkRenderPass render_pass,
 4296:     const VulkanRenderTargetCache::Framebuffer* framebuffer,
 4297:     GpuPassKind pass_kind) {
 4298:   // Blue Dragon FULL native renderer (gpu_bd_native_renderer): redirect BD's
 4299:   // field draws (pitch 720) into the native single-pass RT so the REAL geometry
 4300:   // renders natively - reusing xenia's translated pipelines (RGBA8 is format-
 4301:   // compatible with BD's k_8_8_8_8 field color; load/store ops don't affect
 4302:   // render-pass compatibility). All field draws share this render_pass +
 4303:   // framebuffer, so they stay in ONE held-open pass (no per-tile break, no EDRAM
 4304:   // xfer/resolve) = the pass collapse. Gated, default-off. NEXT: tiling window-
 4305:   // offset handling + bin-once so both tiles land correctly in the one RT.
 4306:   auto bd_rb_surface_info = register_file_->Get<reg::RB_SURFACE_INFO>();
 4307:   // WHOLE-FRAME HLE diagnostic: the redirect catches pitch-720 foliage; the ~800
 4308:   // OPAQUE + other draws still hit LLE EDRAM (the partial-HLE confound). Log the
 4309:   // NON-720 field draws' pitch+msaa to decide the whole-frame architecture: if the
 4310:   // opaque is msaa=0 (1x, like the foliage) the redirect just WIDENS into the same
 4311:   // native pass; if msaa=1 (2x) it needs a SECOND native pass (heterogeneous MSAA).
 4312:   if (cvars::gpu_bd_native_renderer) {
 4313:     uint32_t bd_p = uint32_t(bd_rb_surface_info.surface_pitch);
 4314:     uint32_t bd_m = uint32_t(bd_rb_surface_info.msaa_samples);
 4315:     // Per-frame distribution: count redirected (720) vs non-720 draws by msaa,
 4316:     // logged every 30 swaps so it reflects the FIELD (not boot). Tells the exact
 4317:     // whole-frame HLE scope: how many draws + what MSAA still go to LLE.
 4318:     static std::atomic<uint32_t> s_d720{0}, s_dnz1x{0}, s_dnz2x{0}, s_dnz4x{0};
 4319:     if (bd_p == 720) {
 4320:       s_d720.fetch_add(1);
 4321:     } else if (bd_p >= 256) {
 4322:       if (bd_m == 0) s_dnz1x.fetch_add(1);
 4323:       else if (bd_m == 1) s_dnz2x.fetch_add(1);
 4324:       else s_dnz4x.fetch_add(1);
 4325:     }
 4326:     static std::atomic<uint32_t> s_dist_swap{0};
 4327:     if ((s_dist_swap.fetch_add(1) % 3000u) == 2999u) {
 4328:       XELOGI("BD DRAW DIST (cumulative): pitch720={} non720_1x={} non720_2x={} "
 4329:              "non720_4x={}",
 4330:              s_d720.load(), s_dnz1x.load(), s_dnz2x.load(), s_dnz4x.load());
 4331:     }
 4332:   }
 4333:   bool bd_native_gate = false;
 4334:   // Whether this pass begins the native CLEAR render pass (2 LOAD_OP_CLEAR
 4335:   // attachments = color+depth), so the begin must supply 2 clear values. Missing
 4336:   // them = VUID-VkRenderPassBeginInfo-clearValueCount-00902 -> the Adreno driver
 4337:   // reads null clear values and null-derefs (the on-device crash).
 4338:   bool bd_native_clear_pass = false;
 4339:   // Field color format (A2B10G10R10 = vk 97), computed BEFORE the gate so the
 4340:   // whole-frame path can gate on it.
 4341:   auto bd_color_format =
 4342:       register_file_
 4343:           ->Get<reg::RB_COLOR_INFO>(reg::RB_COLOR_INFO::rt_register_indices[0])
 4344:           .color_format;
 4345:   VkFormat bd_vk_format =
 4346:       render_target_cache_->GetColorVulkanFormat(bd_color_format);
 4347:   // WHOLE-FRAME HLE (gpu_bd_native_whole_frame): MEASURED that the pitch-720 gate
 4348:   // catches only ~40% of draws (the 2x foliage); ~60% (non-720, 1x MSAA opaque)
 4349:   // still hits LLE EDRAM = the perf confound. Catch ALL field-format (vk97) draws
 4350:   // - foliage AND opaque - and force the native pass to 1x so xenia builds matching
 4351:   // 1x pipelines => the WHOLE frame renders in ONE native pass, bypassing LLE for
 4352:   // the opaque majority too. Drops the foliage 2x MSAA (also cheaper). Default off.
 4353:   // Exclude 4x-MSAA field draws (pitch-360, ~28k = a few %) - forcing THOSE to 1x

 8562: void VulkanCommandProcessor::BdL5PublishAlias(uint32_t dest_base,
 8563:                                               uint32_t src_rt_key, uint32_t width,
 8564:                                               uint32_t height,
 8565:                                               VkFormat target_host_format,
 8566:                                               float exp_bias_factor,
 8567:                                               uint32_t swap) {
 8568:   if (cvars::gpu_bd_native_color_lifetime_hle < 5 || !dest_base || !src_rt_key) {
 8569:     return;
 8570:   }
 8571:   // Match the producer whose SOURCE RT key equals this resolve's source (the
 8572:   // native image that actually holds this dest's content). Only if finalized
 8573:   // THIS epoch (content live).
 8574:   auto it = bd_l5_producer_by_srckey_.find(src_rt_key);
 8575:   if (it == bd_l5_producer_by_srckey_.end() ||
 8576:       it->second.view == VK_NULL_HANDLE ||
 8577:       it->second.frame_epoch != bd_l5_frame_epoch_) {
 8578:     return;
 8579:   }
 8580:   BdL5Alias alias = it->second;
 8581:   alias.width = width;
 8582:   alias.height = height;
 8583:   // LEVEL 7 copy-on-resolve (gated >=7, WIP - device-lost under debug): snapshot
 8584:   // the producer's valid rect into a persistent LOGICAL-size image so present +
 8585:   // samplers read correctly-sized frozen content. At =5/=6 present reads the
 8586:   // producer RT directly (the validated breakthrough), no copy.
 8587:   if (cvars::gpu_bd_native_color_lifetime_hle >= 7) {
 8588:     // >=9 enables the format-converting blit slice (target_host_format valid);
 8589:     // <9 keeps the legacy same-format copy (target = UNDEFINED) so =7/=8 behavior
 8590:     // is unchanged and the convert path is opt-in for A/B on desktop.
 8591:     VkFormat convert_target = (cvars::gpu_bd_native_color_lifetime_hle >= 9)
 8592:                                   ? target_host_format
 8593:                                   : VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED;
 8594:     alias.resolved = render_target_cache_->PublishBdNativeResolved(
 8595:         alias.fb, dest_base, width, height, convert_target, exp_bias_factor,
 8596:         swap, bd_l5_frame_epoch_);
 8597:   }
 8598:   bd_l5_alias_by_dest_[dest_base] = alias;
 8599:   if (xe::Clock::QueryGuestUptimeMillis() > 135000) {
 8600:     static std::atomic<uint32_t> s_pub{0};
 8601:     if (s_pub.fetch_add(1) < 40) {
 8602:       XELOGI("L5 ALIAS dest={:08X} src={:08X} gen={} epoch={} {}x{}", dest_base,
 8603:              alias.src_rt_key, alias.generation, alias.frame_epoch, width,
 8604:              height);
 8605:     }
 8606:   }
 8607: }

 8609: VkImageView VulkanCommandProcessor::BdL5LookupAlias(uint32_t guest_base) {
 8610:   if (cvars::gpu_bd_native_color_lifetime_hle < 5 || !guest_base) {
 8611:     return VK_NULL_HANDLE;
 8612:   }
 8613:   auto it = bd_l5_alias_by_dest_.find(guest_base);
 8614:   if (it == bd_l5_alias_by_dest_.end() ||
 8615:       it->second.view == VK_NULL_HANDLE) {
 8616:     return VK_NULL_HANDLE;
 8617:   }
 8618:   // Serve only aliases published in the CURRENT epoch (the double-buffered
 8619:   // frontbuffer: last frame's other-base entry is stale).
 8620:   if (it->second.frame_epoch != bd_l5_frame_epoch_) {
 8621:     return VK_NULL_HANDLE;
 8622:   }
 8623:   // Prefer the logical-size copy-on-resolve snapshot (present's gamma pass reads
 8624:   // it at the correct size); fall back to the producer RT view.
 8625:   if (it->second.resolved &&
 8626:       it->second.resolved->image != VK_NULL_HANDLE) {
 8627:     return it->second.resolved->identity_view;
 8628:   }
 8629:   return it->second.view;
 8630: }

 8632: bool VulkanCommandProcessor::BdL5DropSafe(uint32_t dest_base) {
 8633:   if (cvars::gpu_bd_native_color_lifetime_hle < 6 || !dest_base) {
 8634:     return false;
 8635:   }
 8636:   // NOTE: do NOT require the CURRENT-epoch snapshot here - transfers run in
 8637:   // PerformTransfersAndResolveClears BEFORE this frame's resolve publishes the
 8638:   // snapshot, so it's always null at drop time. The PREV-frame consumer bits
 8639:   // below prove the dest was native-covered + consumed last frame, and coverage
 8640:   // is stable frame-to-frame, so the drop is safe.
 8641:   // Every consumer of this dest LAST frame must have been native (present /
 8642:   // pixel-texture / composite), with NO NonNative reader - else dropping the
 8643:   // EDRAM transfer starves a consumer that still reads the LLE surface.
 8644:   auto it = bd_color_consumer_bits_prev_.find(dest_base);
 8645:   if (it == bd_color_consumer_bits_prev_.end()) {
 8646:     return false;
 8647:   }
 8648:   uint32_t bits = it->second;
 8649:   if (bits & kBdConsumerNonNative) {
 8650:     return false;
 8651:   }
 8652:   return (bits & (kBdConsumerPresent | kBdConsumerPixelTexture |
 8653:                   kBdConsumerComposite)) != 0;
 8654: }

 1523: bool VulkanRenderTargetCache::Resolve(const Memory& memory,

 1529:   written_length_out = 0;

 1537:           IsFixedRGBA16TruncatedToMinus1To1(), resolve_info)) {

 1539:   }

 1541:   // Nothing to copy/clear.

 1544:   }

 1551:       command_processor_.deferred_command_buffer();
 1552: 
 1553:   // Blue Dragon native-draw HLE step 3 (gpu_bd_hle_drop_resolve): BD's field
 1554:   // frame spends ~120ms in ONE GPU fence = the emulated per-tile base-0
 1555:   // EDRAM->RAM resolve copy. When the decoupled full-surface RT is the source of
 1556:   // truth (gpu_bd_hle_present_decoupled), that copy is dead weight - skip its GPU
 1557:   // work (DumpRenderTargets + the per-pixel copy dispatch). Only the COLOR copy
 1558:   // is dropped; depth resolves and clears still run. 1 = base-0 only (BD's
 1559:   // field); 2 = ALL color copies (upper-bound perf probe). On its own (no
 1560:   // decoupled present) it measures the resolve's raw GPU cost against baseline.
 1561:   bool bd_drop_this_resolve = false;
 1562:   if (cvars::gpu_bd_hle_drop_resolve && resolve_info.copy_dest_extent_length &&
 1563:       !resolve_info.IsCopyingDepth()) {
 1564:     if (cvars::gpu_bd_hle_drop_resolve >= 2 ||
 1565:         resolve_info.color_edram_info.base_tiles == 0) {
 1566:       bd_drop_this_resolve = true;

 1568:       if (s_bd_drop_log < 8) {
 1569:         ++s_bd_drop_log;

 1572:             "dest_base={:08X} coord={}x{} mode={}",
 1573:             resolve_info.color_edram_info.base_tiles,
 1574:             resolve_info.copy_dest_base,
 1575:             resolve_info.coordinate_info.width_div_8
 1576:                 << xenos::kResolveAlignmentPixelsLog2,
 1577:             resolve_info.height_div_8 << xenos::kResolveAlignmentPixelsLog2,
 1578:             uint32_t(cvars::gpu_bd_hle_drop_resolve));
 1579:       }
 1580:     }
 1581:   }
 1582:   // REAL-HLE EDRAM deletion (gpu_bd_native_aux_rt): SURGICALLY drop a color resolve
 1583:   // whose dest guest address is now backed by a LIVE native surface (the field
 1584:   // samples that native image via Brick B, so the EDRAM->RAM resolve is dead weight).
 1585:   // Unlike the blunt drop-all-base-0 above (which black-screened with NO native
 1586:   // replacement), this fires ONLY when native content actually serves the dest =
 1587:   // safe. This is what makes the ~110ms EDRAM work redundant.
 1588:   if (!bd_drop_this_resolve && cvars::gpu_bd_native_drop_resolves &&
 1589:       resolve_info.copy_dest_extent_length && !resolve_info.IsCopyingDepth() &&
 1590:       command_processor_.BdNativeSurfaceServes(resolve_info.copy_dest_base)) {
 1591:     bd_drop_this_resolve = true;
 1592:     command_processor_.AddBdNativeResolveDropped();
 1593:     static uint32_t s_bd_native_drop_log = 0;
 1594:     if (s_bd_native_drop_log < 8) {
 1595:       ++s_bd_native_drop_log;
 1596:       XELOGI(

 1598:           "it) ƒ?" EDRAM work deleted for this surface",
 1599:           resolve_info.copy_dest_base);
 1600:     }
 1601:   }
 1602: 
 1603:   // Copying.
 1604:   bool copied = false;
 1605:   if (resolve_info.copy_dest_extent_length && !bd_drop_this_resolve) {
 1606:     // EDRAM-recompiler first brick: record the resolve->sample dependency EDGE -
 1607:     // the dest range PLUS the source RT identity - so a later texture fetch that
 1608:     // lands in this dest range can be routed to the resident source RT directly
 1609:     // (RT-as-texture) or have this resolve deferred (lazy), instead of the
 1610:     // EDRAM->RAM->reload round-trip the increment-1 detector only measured.
 1611:     const bool resolve_is_depth = resolve_info.IsCopyingDepth();
 1612:     const draw_util::ResolveEdramInfo& src_edram =
 1613:         resolve_is_depth ? resolve_info.depth_edram_info
 1614:                          : resolve_info.color_edram_info;
 1615:     VulkanCommandProcessor::ResolveEdge resolve_edge;
 1616:     resolve_edge.dest_start = resolve_info.copy_dest_extent_start;
 1617:     resolve_edge.dest_length = resolve_info.copy_dest_extent_length;
 1618:     resolve_edge.dest_base = resolve_info.copy_dest_base;
 1619:     resolve_edge.src_edram_base_tiles = src_edram.base_tiles;
 1620:     resolve_edge.src_pitch_tiles = src_edram.pitch_tiles;
 1621:     resolve_edge.src_format = src_edram.format;
 1622:     resolve_edge.src_msaa = uint8_t(src_edram.msaa_samples);
 1623:     resolve_edge.src_is_depth = resolve_is_depth;
 1624:     // Pack the FULL source-RT identity (same RenderTargetKey the render draw's
 1625:     // color RT carries) so the native render-redirect can key by it ƒ?" BD renders
 1626:     // every RT at EDRAM base 0, so base alone aliases; pitch+format+msaa

You are a world-class emulator/Vulkan/TBDR engineer giving an independent adversarial design review.

Problem: Xenia fork, Blue Dragon field on AYN Thor, Adreno 740, Mesa Turnip 26.0-devel git-5ac41be677, Vulkan. Goal 30fps. Latest hard on-device fact: gpu frame ~42ms, ~13ms draws and ~30ms between render passes; roughly 43-75 render passes. BD has ~13 logical color/depth surfaces but xenia keys host RTs by Xenos EDRAM layout (base_tiles/pitch_tiles). BD aliases most RTs at EDRAM base 0 and interleaves main 1280x720, shadow, composite, and bloom 320/160/80, so each logical RT is re-begun ~4.7x. Xenia inserts ~35 EDRAM ownership-transfer passes and ~23 resolve dispatches.

A per-surface native conversion approach was just proved catastrophic on Turnip: native producers correct; covered EDRAM color transfers dropped 45->19; but fps fell 10->1.8, 99% GPU. It sampled a float16 (field 4x MSAA) native producer and converted to A2B10 in a separate fullscreen fragment pass. Sampling 4x MSAA forced ~84 MB materialization out of GMEM and the converter added another render pass/store. Therefore no separate conversion/bridge passes.

Directive: resource-keyed native RTs, native texture bindings, delete EDRAM, fuse passes / keep hot RTs GMEM-resident. Turnip advertises dynamic_rendering_local_read, rasterization_order_attachment_access, multisampled_render_to_single_sampled, VK_EXT_custom_resolve, load_store_op_none; no fragment shader interlock.

Repo facts:
- generic RenderTargetCache::RenderTargetKey = EDRAM base + pitch_tiles + msaa + depth/color format; Update derives pitch from RB_SURFACE_INFO.surface_pitch, sizes ownership and ChangeOwnership transfers. Vulkan CreateRenderTarget uses key.GetWidth() and GetRenderTargetHeight() (EDRAM full tile period).
- Current native surfaces are a separate registry keyed only by resolve destination address. Current aux redirect happens late in VulkanCommandProcessor::SubmitBarriersAndEnterRenderTargetCacheRenderPass, after RenderTargetCache::Update and pipeline creation, so cache ownership/layout state is split from actual target.
- Persistent resolve graph currently maps one src_rt_key to one dest, losing same-config/multiple destinations. Consumer redirects expose only base+host format, not full TextureKey.
- Current converter is a separate pass in PublishBdNativeResolved.
- Bundled Vulkan-Headers are 1.3.278 and do not contain VK_EXT_custom_resolve. Xenia logs supported extensions but does not plumb/enable dynamicRenderingLocalRead or multisampledRenderToSingleSampled; ROAA is plumbed.
- Existing feedback/input-attachment merge got only 1/26 and garbled because BD composites use transformed texture coordinates. Local read is same-fragment/framebuffer-local, not arbitrary filtered sampling.
- VK_EXT_custom_resolve is explicitly intended to shader-resolve MSAA in the same render instance, can write a different format, and Turnip implements it by keeping source in GMEM and switching custom-resolve output to sysmem. It can apply average, exp_bias=-2, swap, and A2B10 packing without materializing the MSAA image. Turnip had March 2026 custom-resolve fixes; driver commit ancestry must be checked/upgraded.

624:    // Safety check because a lot of code assumes up to 4x.
625:    assert_always();

632:  // clamp is applied at the resolve path (draw_util::GetResolveInfo), the Vulkan
633:  // render-pass key + framebuffer pitch, and the shader system flags - so the host
634:  // RT key built here and the resolve-time lookup key derive the IDENTICAL sample
635:  // count and the EDRAM tile layout stays coherent (an inconsistent subset desyncs
636:  // tile offsets -> corruption, the failure of the earlier single-site clamp). The
637:  // trace pinned BD's cost to MSAA-2x foliage overdraw (per-sample ROP doubled); 1x
638:  // ~halves it. Default 0 = off; quality trade (loses MSAA edge smoothing).
639:  msaa_samples = draw_util::ClampForcedMsaaSamples(msaa_samples);
640:  uint32_t msaa_samples_x_log2 =
641:      uint32_t(msaa_samples >= xenos::MsaaSamples::k4X);
642:  uint32_t pitch_pixels = rb_surface_info.surface_pitch;
643:  // NOTE: a downstream pitch-widen (360->720) here to force the bin-once RT full-
644:  // width DESYNCS the EDRAM/resolve = 0fps black screen (the goal's warned "harder,
645:  // lossy way"). The clean bin-once must HLE FUN_82487cc8 @0x82487cc8 at the source
646:  // (emit ONE full-width tile + coherent pitch/resolve), not override here.
647:  // surface_pitch 0 should be handled in disabling rasterization (hopefully
648:  // it's safe to assume that).
649:  assert_true(pitch_pixels || !is_rasterization_done);
650:  if (!pitch_pixels) {
651:    is_rasterization_done = false;
652:  } else if (pitch_pixels > xenos::kTexture2DCubeMaxWidthHeight) {
653:    XELOGE(

656:        pitch_pixels, xenos::kTexture2DCubeMaxWidthHeight);
657:    return false;
658:  }

666:        draw_resolution_scale_x();
667:    uint32_t max_render_target_width = GetMaxRenderTargetWidth();
668:    if (pitch_pixels_tile_aligned_scaled > max_render_target_width) {
669:      // TODO(Triang3l): If really needed for some game on some device, clamp
670:      // the pitch and generate multiple ranges (each for every row of tiles)
671:      // with gaps for padding. Very few PowerVR GPUs have 4096, not 8192, as
672:      // the limit, though with 8192 (on Mali) the actual limit for Xenia is
673:      // 8160 because tile padding is stored - but 8192 should be extremely rare
674:      // anyway.

One implementation trap is now explicit in the repo: the current native redirect happens after `RenderTargetCache::Update` and pipeline selection, so Vulkan is told “EDRAM” for ownership/layout/pipeline and then handed a different native framebuffer late. The right architecture is:

```text
guest resource identity
        ↓
resource-keyed native VkImage
        ↓
4x producer stays in GMEM
        ↓  custom resolve inside the same rendering instance
1x native texture in final guest format
        ↓
direct native texture binding
```

EDRAM remains only as a fail-closed fallback. Resource identity deletes ownership-transfer and compute-resolve bridges; custom resolve and compatible “rendering islands” delete tile-store boundaries. A persistent native `VkImage` is not automatically persistent in GMEM.

## 1. Pass fusion and GMEM residency

DXVK/Cemu-style translation does not keep arbitrary framebuffers resident across incompatible RT switches. On Turnip, GMEM belongs to a tiled render job/rendering instance. Ending it and beginning another with different attachments gives the driver a store/load boundary. Turnip may instead choose SYSMEM through its autotuner. [Mesa documents this GMEM/SYSMEM selection explicitly](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/freedreno.html#autotune).

### Dynamic rendering local read

`VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read` is useful, but narrower than “swap arbitrary RTs without ending rendering”:

- All image views are fixed by `vkCmdBeginRendering`.
- It can prebind a superset such as `{A,B}` and remap fragment output location 0 between A and B with `vkCmdSetRenderingAttachmentLocationsKHR`.
- It supports framebuffer-local dependencies and input-attachment reads at overlapping fragment locations.
- It cannot change depth/stencil attachments, perform layout transitions, exceed attachment limits, or express non-framebuffer-space dependencies without splitting rendering.
- It does not turn an attachment into an ordinarily filtered texture. Bloom downscales, transformed UVs and cross-pixel shadow/filter reads still require materialized image contents.

Those restrictions are explicit in the [dynamic-rendering-local-read proposal](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read.html). ROAA only adds ordered access between overlapping fragments; it is not general texture feedback or multi-RT persistence. See [VK_EXT_rasterization_order_attachment_access](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_EXT_rasterization_order_attachment_access.html).

Therefore an original-order `A → B → A` sequence can become one GMEM island only when:

- A and B have compatible render area/extents.
- Their sample configuration is compatible.
- The depth/stencil attachment is fixed.
- Neither sequence ordinarily samples the other between writes.
- No copy, resolve, query-visible operation or layout transition intervenes.
- Their combined bytes-per-pixel do not shrink Turnip’s bin size enough to erase the win.

Prebinding more attachments consumes more GMEM. Turnip can produce smaller bins, more bin iterations, or select SYSMEM, so fewer Vulkan passes on PC is necessary but not sufficient.

### Reordering

Do not begin by reordering shadow/main/bloom draws. Build a resource-version DAG and preserve:

- RAW, WAR and WAW dependencies.
- Partial clears and partial overwrites.
- Predication and queries.
- Order-dependent blending.
- UAV/memexport/shared-memory effects.
- Copies/resolves and guest-memory visibility.
- Depth continuity.

Only reorder independent antichains. A real `shadow write → main samples shadow → shadow rewrite` chain cannot be made contiguous without changing semantics. First form fixed-attachment islands while retaining original order; reorder only after the graph proves independence.

### Load/store policy

The known BD classes are:

| Resource | End-of-producer policy |
|---|---|
| 4x field source | Transient after its in-rendering resolve; no MSAA store |
| 1x field resolve | `STORE`; composite samples it |
| Bloom levels | `STORE`; each is sampled by the next stage/composite |
| Shadow maps | `STORE` until their last consumer |
| Composite/present target | `STORE` |
| Depth | Transient only if never sampled/resolved and all dependent draws stay in one island |
| Dead scratch/full-overwrite generation | `DONT_CARE`/`NONE` |

Every re-begin that must preserve partial contents needs `LOAD`. A later full clear can start with `CLEAR`/`DONT_CARE`.

`STORE_OP_NONE` is not a magic cheaper store for written attachments: once written, it behaves like `DONT_CARE`. Its special value is preserving untouched prior contents without a store access. [The Vulkan reference specifies this distinction](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAttachmentStoreOp.html). Exact classification of all 13 RT generations must come from the frame graph, not dimensions or names.

## 2. MSAA must resolve inside the producer

For the field’s 4x float16 → 1x A2B10 conversion, `VK_EXT_custom_resolve` is the correct Turnip mechanism.

| Mechanism | Good for | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Standard `pResolveAttachments` | Fixed resolve, normally same format | Cannot express float16 → A2B10, exponent bias or swap |
| `VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_single_sampled` | Render directly to a 1x same-format image while N samples exist only on tile | Still fixed-format/fixed resolve semantics |
| `VK_EXT_custom_resolve` | Shader resolve, different destination format, inside the same rendering instance | One resolve draw remains, and final 1x output must be stored |

The [MSRTSS proposal](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_single_sampled.html) says the 1x attachment is represented as N samples during rendering and automatically resolved at the end. Query `VkSubpassResolvePerformanceQueryEXT::optimal` for each candidate format.

For BD, use approximately:

1. Begin dynamic rendering with `VK_RENDERING_CUSTOM_RESOLVE_BIT_EXT`.
2. Bind the 4x float16 producer as the color attachment.
3. Associate a 1x A2B10 native image as `resolveImageView`, with `resolveMode = VK_RESOLVE_MODE_CUSTOM_BIT_EXT`.
4. Use `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_RENDERING_LOCAL_READ_KHR` for the producer and no in-rendering layout transition.
5. Execute all producer draws.
6. Issue a `BY_REGION` color-write → input-attachment-read barrier.
7. Map the multisampled producer as an input attachment.
8. Call `vkCmdBeginCustomResolveEXT`.
9. Draw one no-overdraw fullscreen triangle with the custom-resolve pipeline, reading `subpassInputMS` and performing Xenos averaging, exponent bias, swap and A2B10 packing.
10. End rendering. The 4x attachment uses transient usage and `DONT_CARE`/`NONE`; the 1x native result uses `STORE`.

This is still a resolve draw, but it is not another render pass. Turnip reads the MSAA attachment from GMEM and writes the resolve result directly to its single-sample destination. The [custom-resolve proposal](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_EXT_custom_resolve.html) was specifically designed to avoid tiled renderers spilling the multisampled source, and Turnip’s implementation switches the resolve output to direct SYSMEM rendering while retaining GMEM input attachments ([Mesa source](https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/+/4b87df29b3afcfcdcfe8519f3d47228ca0a4294e%5E%21/)).

It eliminates:

- The full-image 4x MSAA materialization.
- The separate conversion render pass.
- The intervening GMEM store/reload.
- The matching EDRAM resolve/transfer bridge.

It does not eliminate 4x raster/coverage/ROP work, the larger GMEM footprint, or the final necessary 1x store.

However, Xenia currently only plumbs ROAA into device feature discovery/enabling in [vulkan_device.cc](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/ui/vulkan/vulkan_device.cc:195). The bundled Vulkan headers are still 1.3.278 in [vulkan_core.h](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/third_party/Vulkan-Headers/include/vulkan/vulkan_core.h:72) and lack custom-resolve declarations.

So first:

## 3. Resource-keyed native RTs

Yes, `surface_pitch` welding is central to the EDRAM path—but it should not be globally rewritten.

The existing [RenderTargetKey](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/render_target_cache.h:264) intentionally identifies EDRAM storage by base tiles, pitch tiles, MSAA, depth/color and format. `RenderTargetCache::Update` derives that pitch from `RB_SURFACE_INFO.surface_pitch` in [render_target_cache.cc](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/render_target_cache.cc:613), and Vulkan allocation then uses the derived EDRAM width and periodic EDRAM height in [vulkan_render_target_cache.cc](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:2847). Widening only that pitch desynchronizes raster addressing, ownership ranges and resolve addressing—hence the black screen.

Add a parallel model:

```cpp
NativeResourceKey {
  base_address;
  dimension;
  logical_width, logical_height, depth_or_layers;
  guest_pitch;
  texture_format, endian, signedness;
  tiled;
  mip, layer;
  scaled_resolve;
};

NativeResourceVersion {
  NativeResourceKey key;
  uint32_t generation;
  ResolveRect destination_rect;
};

NativeRasterBinding {
  RenderTargetKey edram_layout;   // fallback and guest raster mapping only
  window_offset;
  scissor;
  resolve_source_rect;
  destination_offset;
};
```

The stable key describes storage identity. The generation describes which write is live. The raster binding maps BD’s tile strips into the full logical native image.

`resolve_dest` alone is insufficient because addresses are reused, subresources and rectangles differ, and one EDRAM configuration may resolve to multiple destinations. Xenia already has most of the consumer identity in [TextureCache::TextureKey](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/texture_cache.h:125). Expose/canonicalize that key rather than using the current base-address-plus-format helper in [vulkan_texture_cache.cc](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_texture_cache.cc:736).

Two current structures demonstrate the collisions:

- `NativeSurface` is keyed only by a `uint32_t` resolve address in [bd_native_renderer.h](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/bd_native_renderer.h:35).
- `persistent_resolve_edges_[src_rt_key] = edge` retains only one destination per EDRAM key in [vulkan_command_processor.h](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.h:1832).

Both need versioned, many-to-many resource edges.

### Where native selection belongs

Currently Xenia performs `RenderTargetCache::Update`, then configures the pipeline from its EDRAM render-pass key in [vulkan_command_processor.cc](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:6487). The native aux path redirects the framebuffer later in [the render-pass entry path](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_command_processor.cc:4449). That is structurally split-brain.

The native binding decision must precede `Update`:

1. Resolve `ProducerVersion → NativeResourceVersion`.
2. Pass a `NativeBindingPlan` into `RenderTargetCache::Update`.
3. In native mode, build the render-pass/dynamic-rendering key from the native formats and sample configuration.
4. Skip `ChangeOwnership` and transfer generation for that exact version.
5. Render into the logical native image, retaining guest pitch only for coordinate mapping.
6. At guest resolve:
   - Same-format 1x becomes a version-publication/metadata edge.
   - MSAA or format conversion is already performed through custom resolve.
   - Skip the compute resolve only for the exact covered version.
7. Bind the native view when the complete `TextureKey` matches.
8. Fall back to EDRAM on partial resolves, CPU-visible access, unexpected resource reuse or graph-signature divergence.

The current external conversion path beginning at [PublishBdNativeResolved](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/gpu/vulkan/vulkan_render_target_cache.cc:3678) should disappear, not be optimized.

The fully general solution is D3D HLE: use the guest D3D surface/resource object plus subresource identity at `SetRenderTarget`/resolve time. A PM4-only renderer has lost that object identity and often does not know the future resolve destination when producer draws arrive. The minimal BD path is therefore:

- Learn one frame’s ordered producer-generation → resolve-resource graph on the intact EDRAM path.
- Apply it on the next frame only when the draw/resolve signature matches.
- Fall back immediately on divergence.

Deferred lookahead is also possible—the existing command buffer can patch earlier render-pass targets—but framebuffer patching alone is insufficient; pipeline formats, barriers, ownership and texture bindings must all use the same native plan.

## 4. PC-first build order

Track four separate counters: guest rendering instances, ownership-transfer instances, resolve dispatches and conversion instances.

| Stage | PC proof | Thor-only proof |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Extension plumbing and versioned frame graph | Stable resource DAG; no count reduction expected | Feature-enabled smoke test |
| 1. One 1x same-format resource | Its transfer/resolve events vanish; no replacement pass; attachment history reaches the native consumer | Correct field route; no unexpected SYSMEM regression |
| 2. Remaining 1x color resources | Covered transfer and resolve counters fall monotonically | GPU-frame improvement per covered class |
| 3. Field custom resolve | Separate conversion instance and EDRAM resolve disappear; resolve draw remains inside producer instance; numerical output matches old conversion | No 4x source store; only final 1x output; default autotune selects/benefits from GMEM |
| 4. Native depth generations | Corresponding depth ownership transfers disappear without dropped loads | Correct depth across partial re-begins |
| 5. One compatible `A-B-A` island | Three begin/end regions become one while draw order remains A-B-A | Fewer GMEM loads/stores and net GPU-time win |
| 6. Expand islands and reorder proven-independent nodes | Count approaches the dependency/compatibility lower bound—potentially near the logical RT count | Final tile sizes, GMEM/SYSMEM selection and field performance |

PC can prove:

- Exact producer/consumer resource matching.
- Pass and dispatch-count reduction.
- Attachment history.
- Custom-resolve numerical equivalence.
- Correct partial clears, resource reuse and multi-frame behavior.
- Vulkan validation and layout/barrier correctness.
- Actual BD field pixels through RenderDoc.

Only Thor can prove:

- Whether Turnip selected GMEM or SYSMEM.
- Bin dimensions and whether a larger attachment union increased tile count.
- Actual GMEM load/store elimination.
- Whether the multisample source avoided memory.
- GPU frame time, FPS, thermal behavior and device correctness.

For diagnostic A/Bs, use Turnip’s `prefer_gmem`/`prefer_sysmem` autotune modes; Mesa recommends those over hard `TU_DEBUG=gmem/sysmem` for performance analysis. Production validation must use default autotuning.

## 5. Best first wedges

### First serious performance wedge: field custom resolve

Given that the native field producer already renders correctly, replace only its separate conversion path with in-rendering custom resolve and bind the resulting 1x native image directly in the composite.

This is the smallest slice that attacks the proven catastrophe:

- No separate conversion render pass.
- No 4x MSAA spill.
- No corresponding EDRAM resolve/transfer.
- Exactly one necessary 1x store.

It does not prove arbitrary cross-RT residency, but it proves the most important on-tile MSAA mechanism.

### Second wedge: one compatible A-B-A rendering island

Select the hottest captured A-B-A sequence satisfying the compatibility rules, prebind A and B once, remap output locations, and retain original draw order. PC must show three rendering instances becoming one. Thor must show GMEM selection and fewer store/load events.

This is the clean residency-thesis experiment. If Turnip chooses SYSMEM or the larger attachment union shrinks bins enough to lose performance, do not generalize that island strategy.

### Do not start with the bloom pyramid

The bloom chain changes extent and performs filtered, cross-pixel reads. Dynamic local read cannot fuse those dependencies, and the surfaces are comparatively small. A later single-dispatch compute pyramid may reduce scheduling overhead, but it is a separate algorithmic rewrite and would not validate GMEM-resident RT switching.

So the practical sequence is:

1. Versioned native resource graph and early RTC selection.
2. One 1x identity-format native resource to validate the architecture.
3. Field custom resolve—the first likely Thor gain.
4. One compatible A-B-A island—the direct residency proof.
5. Expand native coverage, then islands, then only dependency-proven reordering.
[2mtokens used[0m
556,210
The right architecture is:

```text
guest resource identity
        ↓
resource-keyed native VkImage
        ↓
4x producer stays in GMEM
        ↓  custom resolve inside the same rendering instance
1x native texture in final guest format
        ↓
direct native texture binding
```

EDRAM remains only as a fail-closed fallback. Resource identity deletes ownership-transfer and compute-resolve bridges; custom resolve and compatible “rendering islands” delete tile-store boundaries. A persistent native `VkImage` is not automatically persistent in GMEM.

## 1. Pass fusion and GMEM residency

DXVK/Cemu-style translation does not keep arbitrary framebuffers resident across incompatible RT switches. On Turnip, GMEM belongs to a tiled render job/rendering instance. Ending it and beginning another with different attachments gives the driver a store/load boundary. Turnip may instead choose SYSMEM through its autotuner. [Mesa documents this GMEM/SYSMEM selection explicitly](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/freedreno.html#autotune).

### Dynamic rendering local read

`VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read` is useful, but narrower than “swap arbitrary RTs without ending rendering”:

- All image views are fixed by `vkCmdBeginRendering`.
- It can prebind a superset such as `{A,B}` and remap fragment output location 0 between A and B with `vkCmdSetRenderingAttachmentLocationsKHR`.
- It supports framebuffer-local dependencies and input-attachment reads at overlapping fragment locations.
- It cannot change depth/stencil attachments, perform layout transitions, exceed attachment limits, or express non-framebuffer-space dependencies without splitting rendering.
- It does not turn an attachment into an ordinarily filtered texture. Bloom downscales, transformed UVs and cross-pixel shadow/filter reads still require materialized image contents.

Those restrictions are explicit in the [dynamic-rendering-local-read proposal](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read.html). ROAA only adds ordered access between overlapping fragments; it is not general texture feedback or multi-RT persistence. See [VK_EXT_rasterization_order_attachment_access](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_EXT_rasterization_order_attachment_access.html).

Therefore an original-order `A → B → A` sequence can become one GMEM island only when:

- A and B have compatible render area/extents.
- Their sample configuration is compatible.
- The depth/stencil attachment is fixed.
- Neither sequence ordinarily samples the other between writes.
- No copy, resolve, query-visible operation or layout transition intervenes.
- Their combined bytes-per-pixel do not shrink Turnip’s bin size enough to erase the win.

Prebinding more attachments consumes more GMEM. Turnip can produce smaller bins, more bin iterations, or select SYSMEM, so fewer Vulkan passes on PC is necessary but not sufficient.

### Reordering

Do not begin by reordering shadow/main/bloom draws. Build a resource-version DAG and preserve:

- RAW, WAR and WAW dependencies.
- Partial clears and partial overwrites.
- Predication and queries.
- Order-dependent blending.
- UAV/memexport/shared-memory effects.
- Copies/resolves and guest-memory visibility.
- Depth continuity.

Only reorder independent antichains. A real `shadow write → main samples shadow → shadow rewrite` chain cannot be made contiguous without changing semantics. First form fixed-attachment islands while retaining original order; reorder only after the graph proves independence.

### Load/store policy

The known BD classes are:

| Resource | End-of-producer policy |
|---|---|
| 4x field source | Transient after its in-rendering resolve; no MSAA store |
| 1x field resolve | `STORE`; composite samples it |
| Bloom levels | `STORE`; each is sampled by the next stage/composite |
| Shadow maps | `STORE` until their last consumer |
| Composite/present target | `STORE` |
| Depth | Transient only if never sampled/resolved and all dependent draws stay in one island |
| Dead scratch/full-overwrite generation | `DONT_CARE`/`NONE` |

Every re-begin that must preserve partial contents needs `LOAD`. A later full clear can start with `CLEAR`/`DONT_CARE`.

`STORE_OP_NONE` is not a magic cheaper store for written attachments: once written, it behaves like `DONT_CARE`. Its special value is preserving untouched prior contents without a store access. [The Vulkan reference specifies this distinction](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAttachmentStoreOp.html). Exact classification of all 13 RT generations must come from the frame graph, not dimensions or names.

## 2. MSAA must resolve inside the producer

For the field’s 4x float16 → 1x A2B10 conversion, `VK_EXT_custom_resolve` is the correct Turnip mechanism.

| Mechanism | Good for | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Standard `pResolveAttachments` | Fixed resolve, normally same format | Cannot express float16 → A2B10, exponent bias or swap |
| `VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_single_sampled` | Render directly to a 1x same-format image while N samples exist only on tile | Still fixed-format/fixed resolve semantics |
| `VK_EXT_custom_resolve` | Shader resolve, different destination format, inside the same rendering instance | One resolve draw remains, and final 1x output must be stored |

The [MSRTSS proposal](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_single_sampled.html) says the 1x attachment is represented as N samples during rendering and automatically resolved at the end. Query `VkSubpassResolvePerformanceQueryEXT::optimal` for each candidate format.

For BD, use approximately:

1. Begin dynamic rendering with `VK_RENDERING_CUSTOM_RESOLVE_BIT_EXT`.
2. Bind the 4x float16 producer as the color attachment.
3. Associate a 1x A2B10 native image as `resolveImageView`, with `resolveMode = VK_RESOLVE_MODE_CUSTOM_BIT_EXT`.
4. Use `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_RENDERING_LOCAL_READ_KHR` for the producer and no in-rendering layout transition.
5. Execute all producer draws.
6. Issue a `BY_REGION` color-write → input-attachment-read barrier.
7. Map the multisampled producer as an input attachment.
8. Call `vkCmdBeginCustomResolveEXT`.
9. Draw one no-overdraw fullscreen triangle with the custom-resolve pipeline, reading `subpassInputMS` and performing Xenos averaging, exponent bias, swap and A2B10 packing.
10. End rendering. The 4x attachment uses transient usage and `DONT_CARE`/`NONE`; the 1x native result uses `STORE`.

This is still a resolve draw, but it is not another render pass. Turnip reads the MSAA attachment from GMEM and writes the resolve result directly to its single-sample destination. The [custom-resolve proposal](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_EXT_custom_resolve.html) was specifically designed to avoid tiled renderers spilling the multisampled source, and Turnip’s implementation switches the resolve output to direct SYSMEM rendering while retaining GMEM input attachments ([Mesa source](https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/+/4b87df29b3afcfcdcfe8519f3d47228ca0a4294e%5E%21/)).

It eliminates:

- The full-image 4x MSAA materialization.
- The separate conversion render pass.
- The intervening GMEM store/reload.
- The matching EDRAM resolve/transfer bridge.

It does not eliminate 4x raster/coverage/ROP work, the larger GMEM footprint, or the final necessary 1x store.

### Xenia plumbing required first

The Thor log advertises local read, custom resolve and MSRTSS ([local-read](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/scratch/thor-debug/bd_doublebuffer_fix_logcat.txt:124), [custom-resolve](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/scratch/thor-debug/bd_doublebuffer_fix_logcat.txt:188), [MSRTSS](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/scratch/thor-debug/bd_doublebuffer_fix_logcat.txt:221)). However, Xenia currently only plumbs ROAA into device feature discovery/enabling in [vulkan_device.cc](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/src/xenia/ui/vulkan/vulkan_device.cc:195). The bundled Vulkan headers are still 1.3.278 in [vulkan_core.h](/C:/Users/leanerdesigner/Documents/New%20project%208/xenia-thor/third_party/Vulkan-Headers/include/vulkan/vulkan_core.h:72) and lack custom-resolve declarations.

So first:

- Upgrade Vulkan-Headers and corresponding function loading.
- Query and enable all three feature structs.
- Load `vkCmdBeginCustomResolveEXT` and attachment-remapping commands.

- Require or verify Turnip ancestry containing the March 2026 dynamic custom-resolve tile-store fix ([Mesa fix](https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/+/67c54c44651016c914b8fc3d60c52a9d5b1a5d3c)), then run a small format-conversion smoke test.

## 3. Resource-keyed native RTs

Yes, `surface_pitch` welding is central to the EDRAM path—but it should not be globally rewritten.
